name: Funnel-Transformer
main_result: B6-6-6H768 vs L12H768: GLUE-avg 85.3 at 0.88x FLOPs (baseline 84.4 at 1.00x)
notes: Strided mean pooling (window 2, stride 2) halves the sequence between blocks; pooled sequence is used only as query (pool-query-only). Decoder up-samples for token-level tasks. Pre-trained from scratch (MLM or ELECTRA) then fine-tuned. Running time on V100 GPU and TPU v2-8 in Appendix C.2 with batch sizes 4-64 per device.
evidence: "we find the simplest strided mean pooling applied to each sliding window of the sequence work very well in practice" (Sec. 2.2); "we empirically evaluate the proposed F-TFM by first pretraining it and then finetuning it in downstream tasks" (Sec. 4)

name: PoWER-BERT
main_result: BERT-base (SST-2): acc 92.1 at 374 ms per batch of 128 on K80 (baseline 93.0 at 905 ms), 2.4x
notes: Score = total attention a word-vector receives (column sum over heads), not only CLS. Retention configuration (count per layer, same for all inputs) learned by soft-extract layers with an L1 mass regularizer. Three steps: fine-tune, configuration search, re-train. Inference time on K80 with batch 128.
evidence: "the significance score is the total amount of attention imposed by w on the other words" (Sec. 3.2); "we design a strategy that learns the retention configuration" (Sec. 3.3); "Given a dataset, the scheme involves three training steps: 1. Fine-tuning ... 2. Configuration-search ... 3. Re-training" (Sec. 3.4)

name: SViTE+
main_result: DeiT-S (SViTE+, 50% unstructured weight sparsity, 95% tokens): top-1 80.18 at 49.32% FLOPs saving (baseline 79.90)
notes: Main contribution is dynamic sparse training of weights (prune-and-grow); SViTE+ adds a learnable token selector (MLP scorer + top-k with Gumbel-softmax straight-through) that drops 5-10% of input tokens. Trained from scratch for 600 epochs. FLOPs given only as % saving, so GFLOPs is unknown. Running time reported as % reduction per iteration in CUDA benchmark mode (4.40% at 95% tokens), device not stated.
evidence: "plugging in a novel learnable token selector to adaptively determine the currently most vital patches" (Abstract); "Then, a selection of the top-k importance scores (1 ≤ k ≤ d) is applied on top of it, aiming to preserve the significant tokens and remove the useless ones" (Sec. 3.2); "we increase training epochs to 600 for all experiments" (Sec. 4)

name: DPS
backbones: thin ResNet of ATS (traffic signs); ResNet-18 (billiard balls); ResNet-50 (CUB, NTS-Net setup)
main_result: ResNet-18 + Transformer aggregation: billiard-balls test acc 93.8 with K=10 selected patches (ResNet-18 on the full image 81.6)
notes: [application] Patch selection for high-resolution recognition whose selected patches go to a CNN feature network, so it is not token reduction inside a ViT. A shallow CNN scorer on a downscaled image scores a grid of patches and a perturbed-maximum differentiable Top-K picks K (5 or 10) patches; sigma decays linearly to 0 during training so inference uses hard Top-K. A small Transformer (3 self-attention layers) is only one of the aggregation options (mean, max, Transformer). The whole model is trained end-to-end; no pre-training of the feature network is mentioned for traffic signs (the paper says pre-training could help), so training is taken as scratch; the CUB setup follows NTS-Net with ResNet-50. Only relative speed is given (hard Top-K 3-10% more images/s; full-image CNN 24% longer training); no FLOPs. The name DPS comes from later work (IPS), not from this paper.
evidence: "we formulate patch selection as a ranking problem, where per-patch relevance scores are predicted by a small ConvNet and the Top K scoring patches are selected for downstream processing" (1. Introduction); "To bridge this we linearly decay σ to zero during training" (4.2); "The whole model is trained end-to-end without any adhoc loss to train the selection module" (Figure 2)

name: Length-Adaptive Transformer
main_result: BERT-base (SQuAD 1.1): F1 88.7 at 0.45x FLOPs (baseline 88.5 at 1.00x)
notes: Uses the PoWER-BERT significance score. LengthDrop trains one model for any length configuration; an evolutionary search picks the configuration for a given FLOPs budget without re-training. Drop-and-Restore keeps dropped vectors aside and restores them at the last layer for token-level tasks. Fig. 3 reports latency vs FLOPs on GPU and CPU at batch 1, 4, 16, 64.
evidence: "We train a transformer with LengthDrop, a structural variant of dropout, which stochastically determines a sequence length at each layer. We then conduct a multi-objective evolutionary search to find a length configuration that maximizes the accuracy and minimizes the efficiency metric under any given computational budget" (Abstract); "Drop-and-Restore, does not eliminate word vectors at each layer according to the length configuration but instead sets them aside until the final hidden layer" (Sec. 3.3)

name: HVT
backbones: HVT-Ti; HVT-S (DeiT-Ti / DeiT-S settings with M pooling stages); Scale HVT-Ti-4
main_result: HVT-S-1: ImageNet-1k top-1 78.00 at 2.40 GFLOPs (DeiT-S 79.80 at 4.60)
notes: Architecture-type method. The DeiT blocks are split into M stages and a 1D max pooling (kernel 3, stride 2) after the first block of each stage halves the sequence, so the token count drops by a fixed pattern with no token scoring. The class token is removed and the prediction uses average pooling. All models are trained from scratch (300 epochs, DeiT recipe). HVT-S-1 is DeiT-S with one pooling stage trained from scratch, so the DeiT-S columns refer to this model. FLOPs only, no throughput.
evidence: "we partition the ViT blocks into several stages and apply the pooling operation (e.g., average/max pooling) in each stage to shrink the sequence length" (Sec. 1); "At the m-th stage, we apply a 1D max pooling operation with a kernel size of k and stride of s to the output of the Transformer block bm" (Sec. 3.2.1); "For experiments on ImageNet, we train our models for 300 epochs with a total batch size of 1024." (Sec. 5)

name: IA-RED2
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.1 at >=1360 fps (baseline 79.8 at <=930 fps, V100)
notes: Multi-head interpreter (policy token dot product with patch tokens, sigmoid) before each of 3 groups of 4 blocks; a patch is dropped if its score is below 0.5, so the count varies per image. Interpreters trained by REINFORCE with an efficiency reward, then the MSA-FFN blocks are fine-tuned, in a curriculum over groups (3 x 30 epochs). Main table gives only fps bounds (>=1360 for IA-RED2, <=930 for DeiT-S; V100-32GB, PyTorch 1.7, batch size not stated), so 1360/930 = 1.46x is a lower bound of the speed-up. GFLOPs for DeiT-S appears only in Appendix D (79.1% at 2.9 G); Table 8 lists 79.1% at 3.4 G for tau=1.5 and SViT Table 7 quotes 3.2 G, so the number is uncertain. Code URL is the project page; no repository link in the paper.
evidence: "adopt a policy network (referred to as multi-head interpreter) to decide which patches are uninformative and then discard them" (Sec. 1); "If Iij is below the threshold 0.5, the patch Xi will be completely discarded at j th group and will not be available in the subsequent groups" (Sec. 3.2); "We optimize the multi-head interpreters by using the REINFORCE method where the reward considers both the efficiency and accuracy, and finetune the MSA-FFN blocks with gradients computed based on cross-entropy loss" (Sec. 3.2)

name: DynamicViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.3 at 2.9 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Keep ratio 0.7 per stage before blocks 4, 7, 10 (0.7, 0.49, 0.34 of tokens). MLP predictor with local and global features; Gumbel-softmax and attention masking in training. 30 epochs from the pretrained model, backbone LR 0.01x, backbone frozen for the first 5 epochs; KL and token distillation from the unpruned model. Throughput on one RTX 3090 with batch 32.
evidence: "we devise a lightweight prediction module to estimate the importance score of each token given the current features" (Abstract); "During inference, we only need to select the most informative tokens according to a predefined pruning ratio and the scores computed by the prediction modules" (Sec. 3.1); "We use the pre-trained vision transformer models to initialize the backbone models and jointly train the whole model for 30 epochs" (Sec. 4)

name: TokenLearner
backbones: ViT-S/32; ViT-B/32; ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16; ViT-L/14; ViT-L/10; ViT-L/8; ViViT
main_result: ViT-B/16 (JFT-300M pretrain, 384px): top-1 83.65 at 28.7 GFLOPs (baseline 84.73 at 55.6)
notes: 8 or 16 tokens generated by S spatial attention maps (conv or MLP) applied to the input and spatially pooled; inserted at the middle of the network (or later); TokenFuser maps back to the original shape. Pre-trained on JFT-300M with TokenLearner inserted, then fine-tuned on ImageNet, so numbers are not comparable with DeiT. Runtime: ViT-L/16 1400 vs 2000 images/s with TokenLearner (device not stated).
evidence: "TokenLearner is a learnable module that takes an image-like tensor (i.e., input) and generates a small set of tokens" (Sec. 1); "We compute spatial attention maps highlighting regions-of-importance (using convolutional layers or MLPs), and they are applied to the input itself to weight each region differently (and discard unnecessary regions). The results are spatially pooled to generate the final learned tokens" (Sec. 1); "we pre-train the model with JFT and fine-tune it with the original ImageNet dataset" (Sec. 3.4)

name: DGE
main_result: PVT-S: top-1 80.2 at 3.5 GFLOPs (baseline 80.2 at 6.2)
notes: Each S x S region gets a granularity (1, 2 or 4) from a gating network; patches are average pooled into queries, keys/values stay dense, output is un-pooled to full resolution with a residual. Budget loss with target ratio gamma=0.5 during training; per-image count varies. All models re-trained 300 epochs at 256x256. DeiT-S+DGE appears only in Fig. 5 (no number in text). Latency on Xeon 6130 CPU and V100 GPU for one 800x1280 (COCO) or 512x2048 (ADE20k) image.
evidence: "For each region, the number of patches is decided by a data-dependent routing process, and each patch is average pooled to obtain a 1D token" (Sec. 1); "we define a computational budget denoted as γ ∈ [0, 1], which corresponds to the desired computational complexity ratio relative to the vanilla encoder without dynamic grained" (Sec. 3.2.3); "All the models are trained for 300 epochs with 128 images per batch" (Sec. 4.1.1)

name: DVT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.4 at 2.90 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.61)
notes: Cascade of transformers with 7x7, 10x10, 14x14 tokens; exit when the max softmax probability reaches a threshold; thresholds solved by a genetic algorithm for a FLOPs budget. Feature and relationship reuse between stages. Criterion is prediction confidence, not a token score. Trained with the backbone recipe (initialization from pretrained weights not mentioned). Throughput only for T2T-ViT on a 2080Ti with batch 128.
evidence: "This is achieved by cascading multiple Transformers with increasing numbers of tokens, which are sequentially activated in an adaptive fashion at test time, i.e., the inference is terminated once a sufficiently confident prediction is produced" (Abstract); "we simply train DVT to produce correct predictions at all exits" (Sec. 3.1); "The training of DVT follows exactly the same configurations as the backbones" (Appendix A)

name: PnP-DETR
backbones: ResNet-50; ResNet-50-DC5; ResNet-101 (DETR); hybrid ResNet-50 + ViT (PnP-ViT)
main_result: DETR-R50-DC5 COCO: AP 42.7 at 20.7 GFLOPs transformer (baseline 43.3 at 74.0), poll ratio 0.33
notes: Reduction is on the CNN feature map before the DETR transformer. The poll sampler (2-layer MLP score) keeps the top alpha*HW tokens (fine set, modulated by the score); the pool sampler aggregates all non-sampled tokens with learned attention weights into M coarse tokens (M = 60 or 240). For panoptic segmentation the encoder output is projected back to the 2D map (reverse projection). Random poll ratio training lets one model run at several ratios. The detector is trained end to end with the DETR recipe. Inference time on TITAN RTX (encoder 17.4 vs 72.4 ms); batch size not stated. FLOPs exclude the backbone.
evidence: "We use a small meta-scoring network to predict the informativeness score for each spatial feature location (i, j)" (Sec. 3.3); "the pool sampler then dynamically aggregates the remaining non-sampled feature vectors into a small number of coarse feature vectors" (Sec. 3.3); "we observe that fixed amount sampling already generates good performance, i.e., N = αL where α is a constant fractional value, which we name as the poll ratio" (Sec. 3.3); "The resulting models are end-to-end learned and other settings are the same with original models." (Sec. 3.4)

name: TR-BERT
main_result: BERT-base (SQuAD 2.0): F1 75.66 at 2.08x FLOPs speedup (baseline 77.12)
notes: Policy network (2-layer FFN) trained by REINFORCE with imitation warm-up, then whole network fine-tuned; two reduction modules (before layers 2 and 6). Skipped tokens keep their last representation for prediction. Count varies per input; the inference-time decision rule is not stated, so schedule is set to other. Wall time: 2.08x FLOPs gives 2.01x on V100 with batch 32.
evidence: "TR-BERT employs the reinforcement learning (RL) method to learn the dynamic token selection strategy automatically" (Sec. 1); "(3) Unfreeze all parameters and train the entire network with the task-specific objective and RL objective simultaneously" (Sec. 3.2)

name: PS-ViT
main_result: PS-ViT-B/10: top-1 80.6 at 3.1 GFLOPs, 1348.0 img/s (DeiT-S 79.8 at 4.6 GFLOPs, 1018.2 img/s)
notes: [core] Learned token sampling replaces the fixed ViT patch grid, and the sampling number n sets the sequence length (n=10 gives 100 tokens; the default n=14 gives 196, the same as ViT/16 at 224). A ResNet-50 stem gives a feature map; for N=4 iterations a transformer layer predicts sampling offsets and tokens are re-sampled by bilinear interpolation; a ViT module then processes the n x n tokens. Token count is fixed per model. Trained from scratch on ImageNet-1k for 300 epochs with the DeiT recipe. Throughput on one 32GB V100, batch 128. No pruned DeiT-S setting, so the DeiT-S columns are empty; the gain over DeiT comes from both the CNN stem and the sampling.
evidence: "At each iteration, embeddings of the current sampling step are fed into a transformer encoder layer, and a group of sampling offsets is predicted to update the sampling locations for the next step" (Abstract); "The number of sampling points along each spatial dimension n is set as 14 by default" (3.3); "We train our proposed PS-ViT on ImageNet without pretraining on large-scale datasets" (4.1)

name: ACT
main_result: DETR-DC5 COCO: AP 42.6 at +58.2 GFLOPs over the backbone (baseline 43.3 at +73.4), ACT L=32 training-free; 43.1 with MTKD
notes: Only the queries of encoder self-attention are clustered: E2LSH hashing groups similar queries into prototypes (mean), attention is computed for prototypes against all keys, and the output is broadcast back to every query in the group, so the full token sequence is kept for keys, values and FFN. The number of prototypes follows the hash buckets and varies per image and layer (controlled by the number of hash rounds L). Training-free ACT; MTKD fine-tunes the pre-trained DETR for 5 + 2 epochs. Inference time on GTX TITAN X with batch size 1.
evidence: "ACT clusters the query features adaptively using Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) and approximates the query-key interaction using the prototype-key interaction." (Abstract); "Then, we get the target vector for each prototype and broadcast it to each original query." (Sec. 3.2); "Our method adaptively determines the number of prototypes so that these disadvantages can be avoided." (Sec. 4.4); "ACT can be a drop-in module replacing the original self-attention module without any training." (Abstract); "MTKD performs fine-tuning over the pre-trained model for 5 epochs with the learning rate of 10−5 and continues running for 2 epochs by reducing the learning rate by 1/10." (Sec. 4.2)

name: ATS
backbones: DeiT-S; CvT-13; CvT-21; PS-ViT-B/14; PS-ViT-B/18; XViT; TimeSformer
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.7 at 2.9 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6), after 30-epoch fine-tuning
notes: Score = CLS attention weight times ||V_j||, summed over heads; parameter-free. Tokens chosen by inverse transform sampling over the score CDF with at most K samples; duplicates removed, so the count K' varies per image (schedule set to other because there is no threshold). Training-free use on a pretrained DeiT-S: about 0.6% drop (Appendix C); fine-tuned variant: 30 epochs following the DynamicViT setup. Multi-stage: ATS in blocks 3-11. Throughput on an RTX 6000 (batch size not stated). Code URL is the project page.
evidence: "Since ATS is a parameter-free module, it can be added to the off-the-shelf pre-trained vision transformers as a plug and play module, thus reducing their GFLOPs without any additional training. Moreover, due to its differentiable design, one can also train a vision transformer equipped with ATS" (Abstract); "If a token is sampled more than once, we only keep one instance. As a consequence, the number of unique indices K ′ is often lower than K" (Sec. 3.2)

notes: [analysis] Survey, not a method: reviews dynamic neural networks in three groups (sample-wise, spatial-wise with pixel-, region- and resolution-level adaptation, temporal-wise for video and text). Written mainly about CNNs and RNNs; dynamic vision Transformers with early exiting or token sparsification appear only as a future direction (Sec. 7.2). Useful as background for input-adaptive computation, early exit and token skimming. Target set to other because the survey covers images, video and text.
evidence: "In this survey, we comprehensively review this rapidly developing area by dividing dynamic networks into three main categories" (Abstract); "recent work has proposed dynamic vision Transformers with adaptive early exiting [271] or token sparsification [272], [273]" (7.2)

name: MSHViT (Sinkhorn tokenizer)
notes: Only the abstract was available (ScienceDirect and the Aalborg University repository blocked automated download). A CNN backbone is extended with a lightweight ViT that aggregates multi-scale features non-locally; a Sinkhorn clustering-based tokenizer with distinct cluster centers produces a smaller set of tokens. Evaluated on Sewer-ML multi-label sewer defect classification (up to +2.53 points). Token count, training, backbones and costs could not be checked. Application paper in which token reduction is part of the tokenizer.
evidence: "This paper describes the multi-scale hybrid vision transformer (MSHViT), an extension of the classical convolutional neural network (CNN) backbone, for multi-label sewer defect classification" (Abstract); "a smaller set of tokens was produced through a novel Sinkhorn clustering-based tokenizer using distinct cluster centers" (Abstract)

name: LTP
main_result: RoBERTa-base (QQP): acc 89.69 at 2.53 GFLOPs (baseline 90.39 at 5.31), 2.10x
notes: Score = column mean of attention probability averaged over heads (attention received from all tokens). Per-layer thresholds learned with a soft sigmoid mask and an L1 regularizer; then mask binarized and model fine-tuned. Throughput up to 1.9x on V100 and 2.0x on Intel Haswell CPU (Fig. 6, several batch sizes; the batch sizes are not given in the text, so batch1 is unknown).
evidence: "LTP prunes tokens with an attention score below a threshold, whose value is learned for each layer during training" (Abstract); "After (i) jointly training model parameters and thresholds on downstream tasks with the soft pruning scheme, (ii) we fix the thresholds and binarize the soft mask, and (iii) perform a follow-up fine-tuning of the model parameters" (Sec. 3.3)

name: SPViT
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M; PiT-T/XS/S; Swin-T/S
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.34 at 2.64 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6); latency 60 ms vs 113 ms on a Samsung Galaxy S20
notes: Multi-head token selector (per-head MLP scores combined by a head-attention branch) with Gumbel-softmax; less informative tokens packed into one package token. A latency-sparsity look-up table of the target device sets per-block pruning rates through a latency-aware sparsity loss; per-image rates vary around the target. Layer-to-phase progressive training, selectors after layers 3/6/9; 60 epochs from pretrained weights. Latency on a Snapdragon 865 mobile CPU and a Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA (13.23 ms); no GPU throughput; batch size of the latency measurement not stated.
evidence: "We further introduce a soft pruning technique, which integrates the less informative tokens chosen by the selector module into a package token rather than discarding them completely" (Abstract); "we introduce the latency-aware sparsity loss to obtain the pruning rate of token constrained by the latency specifications of the target devices" (Sec. 4.3); "We follow most of the training settings as in DeiT and train all backbone models for 60 epochs" (Sec. 5)

name: EViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.5 at 3.0 GMACs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Keep rate 0.7 at layers 4, 7, 10; CLS attention averaged over heads; inattentive tokens fused into one token by attention-weighted average. Trained from scratch for 300 epochs (keep rate warmed up with a cosine schedule); also fine-tunes from a pretrained DeiT with an oracle (Table 6) and at higher resolution. Cost is reported as MACs (torchprofile), entered in the GFLOPs column. Throughput on one A100 with batch 128.
evidence: "we identify the attentive image tokens between MHSA and FFN (i.e., feed-forward network) modules, which is guided by the corresponding class token attention. Then, we reorganize image tokens by preserving attentive image tokens and fusing inattentive ones" (Abstract); "We train the models with EViT from scratch for 300 epochs on 16 NVIDIA A100 GPUs" (Sec. 4)

name: Expedite
backbones: ViT-L/16; ViT-B/16 (Segmenter); R50+ViT-B/16 (DPT); SwinV2-L (HTC++); Swin-L (Mask2Former); SWAG ViT-L/16, ViT-H/14 (classification)
main_result: Segmenter ViT-L/16 ADE20K: mIoU 51.56 at 438.9 GFLOPs (baseline 51.82 at 659.0), 28x28 clusters
notes: The paper names no method (Expedite is how AiluRus and Token Adapter call it). A token clustering layer after layer alpha (=10 for ViT-L) runs local k-means (SLIC style, init by adaptive average pooling) to h x w cluster tokens; the following beta layers run on the clusters; a non-parametric token reconstruction layer maps them back to all positions by the same soft similarity weights before the dense head. Cluster size and positions are fixed hyper-parameters. FPS on one V100; batch size not stated. The NeurIPS checklist says the code will be released soon; no URL in the paper.
evidence: "we present two non-parametric operators, a token clustering layer to decrease the number of tokens and a token reconstruction layer to increase the number of tokens" (Abstract); "We construct the token clustering layer following the improved SLIC scheme [33], which performs local k-means clustering as follows" (Sec. 3); "Therefore, we choose 28 × 28 on Segmenter+ViT-L/16 by default." (Sec. 4.3); "We can integrate the proposed token clustering layer and token reconstruction layer seamlessly with the provided official trained checkpoints with no further fine-tuning required." (Sec. 4)

name: PPT
main_result: PPT-S COCO val: AP 72.2 at 1.6 GFLOPs / 842 im/s (TokenPose-S 72.5 at 2.2 GFLOPs / 651 im/s), keep ratio 0.7
notes: Human pose estimation (top-down, keypoint tokens as in TokenPose). The Human Token Identification module sums the attention of all keypoint tokens to each visual token and keeps the top r = 0.7 visual tokens before layers 4, 7, 10 (2, 4, 5 for L/D6); pruned tokens are not restored because heatmaps come from the keypoint tokens. Trained for 300 epochs with the TokenPose recipe; keep ratio annealed from 1 to r in the first 100 epochs. Throughput on one 2080 Ti with batch 32; FPS (single instance) barely changes (120 vs 123). Multi-view PPT fuses only the kept human tokens across views.
evidence: "we propose the Human Token Identification module to select informative visual tokens with the help of attention scores of keypoint tokens" (Sec. 3.1); "we keep visual tokens with the K largest corresponding values in a as the human tokens, and prune the remaining tokens" (Sec. 3.1); "the keep ratio r is set to 0.7 by default" (Sec. 4.1); "all networks are optimized by Adam optimizer [25] with Mean Square Error (MSE) loss for 300 epochs" (Sec. 4.1)

name: AdaViT
main_result: T2T-ViT-19: top-1 81.1 at 3.9 GFLOPs (baseline 81.9 at 8.5)
notes: A decision network before each block predicts keep/drop for patches, attention heads and the MSA/FFN sub-layers; Gumbel-softmax in training with a usage loss toward budgets gamma_p, gamma_h, gamma_b; binary decisions by thresholding at inference, so the count varies per image. Backbone initialized from pretrained T2T-ViT and trained 150 epochs. Only FLOPs reported. Paper says the code will be released; no URL.
evidence: "a light-weight decision network is attached to the backbone to produce decisions on-the-fly" (Abstract); "As the decisions are binary, the action of keeping / discarding can be selected by simply applying a threshold on the entries during inference" (Sec. 3.2); "We initialize the transformer backbone of AdaViT with the pretrained weights released in the official implementation of [50]" (Sec. 4.1)

name: STAM
main_result: DeiT-S (distilled): ImageNet top-1 76.35 with 20.5K pixels sensed (19 glimpses of 32x32; PatchDrop 76.00 with 27.9K)
notes: Reinforcement learning (one-step actor-critic). The agent never sees the full image: it senses one 32x32 glimpse (4 patches of 16x16) per step at a location chosen by an actor MLP from past glimpses, and only the patches of the sensed glimpses enter DeiT, so the token count is 4 x the number of glimpses. Default T=21 steps; an optional early-termination rule stops when the max class probability exceeds gamma (66.47% at 7.5 glimpses on average for gamma=0.5). Core initialized from pre-trained DeiT-distilled and trained 200 epochs on ImageNet with a consistency loss to a full-image teacher. Cost is given as pixels sensed, not FLOPs; no throughput. Active-vision (glimpse) method rather than token reduction inside a ViT.
evidence: "STAM sequentially observes informative glimpses (gt ) from an image. While never observing an image entirely, STAM predicts the class-label of an image (y) based on glimpses" (Fig. 1); "we adopt one-step actor-critic algorithm [41] to update the parameters at each time step" (4.2); "We initialize the core and the classifiers using a pretrained DeiTD" (5. Implementation); "Our agent runs for T = 21 time-steps per image, capturing one glimpse at a time" (5. Optimization)

name: PatchMerger
backbones: ViT-S/32; ViT-B/32; ViT-L/32; ViT-L/16; ViT-H/14; ViT-H/11; V-MoE (S/32 to H/14)
main_result: ViT-H/14 (JFT-300M pretraining): same JFT precision@1 and ImageNet 10-shot accuracy as ViT-H/14 at 51.6% of the FLOPs and 63.5% of the runtime
notes: A single merger after the first half of the blocks maps any number of input tokens to a fixed M=8 output tokens: each patch gets M scores from a learned linear map, softmax over the scores, and the outputs are the score-weighted sums (fixed learned queries, like TokenLearner). Trained from scratch on JFT-300M, then few-shot or fully fine-tuned on ImageNet; no DeiT-S and no ImageNet-1k-only training. Runtime is reported as total training runtime (appendix figures), hardware not stated in the text.
evidence: "outputs a fixed number of tokens when applied to any number of input tokens" (Sec. 3); "computes M scores s1:M (p) — one per output patch — based on a linear transformation of the patch representation at that point" (Sec. 3); "we place one merger layer in the middle of the network, and it outputs 8 patches" (Sec. 4); "We train all of our models on JFT (Hinton et al., 2015), a proprietary dataset containing 300M images." (Sec. 4)

name: Sparse DETR
main_result: Swin-T Deformable DETR COCO: AP 48.2 at 113 GFLOPs / 21.2 FPS (baseline 48.0 at 185 GFLOPs / 15.4 FPS), keep ratio 10%
notes: Tokens are the multi-scale backbone features entering the Deformable DETR encoder. Unselected tokens are not updated but pass through every encoder layer and serve as keys, so no reactivation is needed for the decoder. A 4-layer scoring network is trained with BCE against the binarized decoder cross-attention map (DAM); an objectness-score variant is also reported. The whole detector is trained for 50 epochs with the Deformable DETR recipe (ImageNet-pretrained backbone). FPS measured as in Deformable DETR; batch size for FPS not stated.
evidence: "For features that are not updated in this process, the values of xfeat are passed through the encoder layers without being changed." (Sec. 3.2); "we consider a 4-layer scoring network g to predict how likely a given encoder token is included in the top-ρ % most referenced tokens, and the network is trained by minimizing the binary cross entropy (BCE) loss between the binarized DAM and prediction" (Sec. 3.3); "We then define ρ-salient regions Ωρs as the top-ρ% tokens with the highest scores, for a given keeping ratio ρ" (Sec. 3.2); "We train the model on a 4×V100 GPU machine with a total batch size of 16, for 50 epochs" (Sec. 4)

name: PS-ViT (Patch Slimming)
backbones: DeiT-Ti; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; T2T-ViT-14; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.4 at 2.6 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Top-down: patches kept in layer l+1 are also kept in layer l. Impact score of a patch = effect on the last-layer reconstruction error, computed from products of attention maps of the deeper layers (Theorem 1) and averaged over a data subset, so the mask is static (same for all images). Count per layer set by a tolerant error eps. Each block is fine-tuned for 3 epochs after selection, then the whole model is fine-tuned. Dynamic variant DPS-ViT adds a small predictor per block (79.5 at 2.4 G). Throughput device and batch size not stated (experiments on V100). No code URL in the paper.

For each layer, the impact of a patch on the final output feature is approximated and patches with less impact will be removed" (Abstract); "After pruning, the mask ml is fixed, and weight parameters in the vision transformer is further fine-tuned to be compatible with the efficient architecture" (Sec. 4.3)

name: STTS
main_result: MViT-B16 Kinetics-400: top-1 78.1 at 0.28 TFLOPs (baseline 78.4 at 0.35 TFLOPs); single view 56.4 GFLOPs at 96.5 video/s (baseline 70.5 GFLOPs at 79.3 video/s)
notes: Tokens are the 3D cube embeddings of MViT / VideoSwin. Temporal selection keeps the top-K frames (frame scores from spatially pooled tokens); spatial selection keeps one anchor region per frame so the 2D structure survives pooling. The scorer is a 2-layer MLP trained end-to-end with a perturbed-maximum differentiable Top-K; the selection ratio is fixed. Pretrained backbone fine-tuned (20 epochs for MViT, backbone lr 0.01x of the modules). Throughput measured on an 8x RTX 3090 server; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we formulate token selection as a ranking problem, which estimates the importance of each token through a lightweight scorer network and only those with top scores will be used for downstream evaluation" (Abstract); "This also allows us to explicitly control how many tokens are used." (Sec. 1); "In our experiments, we finetune the pre-trained video transformers with our STTS modules." (Sec. 4.1)

name: VTC-LFC
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.4 at 54.4% FLOPs reduction (baseline 79.8)
notes: Joint channel and token pruning. Token score combines low-frequency energy (LFE) with head-weighted CLS attention; channels are scored by low-frequency sensitivity (Taylor). Bottom-up cascade pruning sets per-block token and channel counts offline on 5000 training images under an allowed accuracy drop (same for every image); then 150-epoch fine-tuning (DeiT-S) with hard distillation. Table 1 gives only the FLOPs reduction ratio, Table 6 gives 2.1 GFLOPs for the same 79.4% model. Throughput on one V100, batch 256. Not RL.
evidence: "Two metrics named low-frequency sensitivity (LFS) and low-frequency energy (LFE) are proposed for better channel pruning and token pruning" (Abstract); "During compression of each block, the number of tokens is gradually reduced until the performance drop reaches" (Bottom-up Cascade Pruning); "After pruning, the compressed models are fine-tuned with hard distillation" (Sec. 4)

name: Evo-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.4 at 1510 img/s (baseline 79.8 at 940 img/s, V100 batch 256)
notes: Global class attention (residual over layers) selects top-k (ratio 0.5) from layer 5. Placeholder tokens are summed into one representative token that goes through MSA/FFN with the informative tokens; the placeholder tokens are kept and fast-updated by copying the representative token's residual, so the 2D structure is preserved (halt part). 300 epochs from scratch with a layer-to-stage schedule. No FLOPs reported, only throughput.
evidence: "we conduct unstructured instance-wise token selection by taking advantage of the simple and effective global class attention that is native to vision transformers" (Abstract); "the placeholder tokens are summarized to a representative token that is evolved via the full transformer encoder simultaneously with the informative tokens in a slow and elaborate way. Then, the evolved representative token is exploited to fast update the placeholder tokens" (Sec. 1); "For fair comparisons, all the models are trained for 300 epochs" (Experiments, Setup)

name: OSTrack
main_result: OSTrack-384 LaSOT: AUC 71.1 at 48.3 GMACs / 58.1 FPS (without elimination 71.0 at 65.3 GMACs / 41.4 FPS)
notes: Single object tracking: the main contribution is the one-stream tracker, and candidate elimination is an add-on. Search-region tokens (target candidates) are ranked by the head-averaged attention from the center template token; the top 70% are kept at layers 4, 7 and 10; template tokens are never removed. Eliminated candidates are zero-padded back as placeholders for the box head (not restored). The tracker is trained from a MAE-pretrained ViT-B. Speed on one RTX 2080 Ti; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we only keep the candidates corresponding to the k largest (top-k) elements" (Sec. 3.2); "This is fairly reasonable as the center template part has aggregated enough information through self-attention to represent the target." (Sec. 3.2); "we first restore the order of the remaining candidates and then zero-pad in between them" (Sec. 3.2); "The keeping ratio ρ of each candidate elimination module is set as 0.7, and a total of three candidate elimination modules are inserted at layers 4, 7, and 10 of ViT respectively" (Sec. 4.1); "The vanilla ViT-Base [12] model pre-trained with MAE [17] is adopted as the backbone" (Sec. 4.1)

name: A-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 78.6 at 3.6 GFLOPs (baseline 78.9 at 4.6, DeiT-S fine-tuned without distillation)
notes: Halting score = sigmoid of one embedding dimension of each token (no extra parameters); a token is removed once its cumulative score reaches 1-eps; ponder loss plus a distributional prior on the exit depth. 100 epochs fine-tuning from pretrained DeiT without mixup or distillation token (with distillation token: 80.7). Throughput given as 1.1K imgs/s on an RTX 2080 with batch 64. Code URL is the project page.
evidence: "A token is discarded once reaching the halting condition" (Fig. 1 caption); "we conduct the token stopping when the cumulative halting score exceeds 1 − ε" (Sec. 3); "Starting from publicly available pretrained checkpoints, we fine-tune DeiT-T/S variant models for 100 epochs" (Sec. 4)

name: MIA-Former
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.9 at 3.9 GFLOPs (head, depth and token skipping; baseline 79.9 at 4.6)
notes: Reinforcement learning (A2C) in a hybrid supervised + RL scheme. A MIA-Controller before each block (CNN/MLP + Gumbel softmax, then A2C actor-critic heads) skips whole blocks, heads and tokens per input; masked tokens pass through a skip connection (operation other, closest to a per-block halt). Training: controller pretraining with blocks fixed, 200-epoch co-training with a FLOPs target, then A2C fine-tuning of controller and blocks from the pre-trained ViT. The reported 79.9 at 3.9 GFLOPs skips heads, blocks and tokens. Token-only skipping gives 79.7 at 3.8 GFLOPs (Table 2). The paper's own unreduced DeiT-S is 79.9 at 4.6 GFLOPs (Table 2), not 79.8. RL stage: 20 epochs plus 50 epochs joint. FLOPs only, no throughput. No code URL.
evidence: "our MIA-Former adopts a low-cost network trained with a hybrid supervised and reinforcement training method to skip unnecessary layers, heads, and tokens in an input adaptive manner" (Abstract); "Note that a skip connection is also added to pass the information of masked heads and tokens to the outputs of the next block" (MIA-Former Framework); "we use an A2Cbased (Mnih et al. 2016) RL learning method to train the MIA-Controller and MIA-Block modules" (Skipping Policy Finetuning with Hybrid RL)

name: TCFormer
main_result: TCFormer: ImageNet-1k top-1 82.4 at 5.9 GFLOPs (25.6M params; DeiT-S 79.9 at 4.6); COCO-WholeBody whole-body AP 57.2
notes: New hierarchical architecture, not a plug-in. The CTM block between stages clusters tokens with DPC-KNN on token features and merges each cluster by an importance-weighted average (importance score P predicted from the features), then merged tokens attend to the original ones. Cluster number fixed to a quarter of the input tokens per stage. ImageNet model trained from scratch for 300 epochs. No DeiT-S results. No latency numbers; the paper only says clustering and merging take 9.4% of the forward time and that DPC-KNN is quadratic in the token number.
evidence: "which merges tokens by progressive clustering, where the tokens can be merged from different locations with flexible shapes and sizes" (Abstract); "we utilize a variant of k-nearest neighbor based density peaks clustering algorithm (DPC-KNN)" (Sec. 3.3); "we set the cluster number to a quarter of the input token number" (Sec. 3.5); "TCFormer without the MTA head is trained from scratch for 300 epochs" (Sec. 4.4)

name: SiT
main_result: LV-ViT-S (SiT-S): top-1 83.2 at 4.0 GFLOPs, 1892 img/s (baseline 83.3 at 6.6, 1360 img/s, V100)
notes: Token Slimming Module: X_hat = A X with A = softmax(W_q sigma(X W_k)^T / tau), a learned N_hat x N soft aggregation (keep ratio 0.5), inserted three times. Feature Recalibration Distillation: a reverse module reconstructs full tokens for block-wise distillation from the unslimmed teacher. DeiT-S numbers from Table 1 (79.4 at 3308 img/s, +102.1% over the unreduced DeiT-S at 79.8 and 1637 img/s; the row at 79.8 and 2344 img/s is a second SiT variant). name: IPS
backbones: ResNet-18 (ImageNet-1k, traffic signs); ResNet-50 BYOL features (CAMELYON16)
main_result: ResNet-50 BYOL features: CAMELYON16 AUC 98.1 with M=5k selected from all patches, 4.7 GB VRAM, 355 ms per training step (batch 16)
notes: [application] Memory-efficient patch selection for megapixel and gigapixel images (traffic signs, megapixel MNIST, CAMELYON16 whole-slide images) with a CNN patch encoder and a cross-attention aggregator, so it is not token reduction inside a ViT. In no-gradient mode IPS scans patches I at a time and keeps the top-M by the cross-attention score of a learnable query token; only the M kept patches are re-embedded with gradients and aggregated. M is fixed per run (2 to 5k). Traffic-sign encoder is an ImageNet ResNet-18 fine-tuned; CAMELYON16 uses features extracted by a BYOL ResNet-50 and trains the aggregator. Runtime is training forward+backward time on one A100 with batch 16; no inference latency.
evidence: "an iterative patch selection module that selects a fixed number of patches and a transformer-based patch aggregation module that combines patch embeddings to compute a global image embedding" (2 Methods); "They both share the cross-attention layer" (2.2); "a ResNet-18 with ImageNet-1k weights is used as encoder for all methods and then finetuned" (4.1)

name: ToMe
backbones: ViT-S/B/L (AugReg); ViT-L/H (SWAG); ViT-B/L/H (MAE); DeiT-Ti; DeiT-S; ViT-L (spatiotemporal MAE, Kinetics-400); ViT-B (AudioMAE)
main_result: DeiT-S trained from scratch with ToMe r=13: top-1 79.4 at 2.7 GFLOPs, 1552 im/s (baseline 79.8 at 4.6, 930 im/s); off-the-shelf AugReg ViT-S r=13: 79.3 at 2.7 GFLOPs, 1550 im/s
notes: Bipartite soft matching: tokens split into two sets by alternation, each token in A linked to its most similar token in B by cosine similarity of the attention keys (averaged over heads), the r most similar edges merged by size-weighted averaging; placed between attention and MLP; proportional attention adds log(size) to the logits. Fixed r per block for every image (constant or decreasing schedule). Works off-the-shelf without training; training with ToMe reduces the drop (MAE fine-tuning, DeiT trained from scratch 300 epochs). The DeiT-S row in Table 4 is trained from scratch, not fine-tuned. Throughput on a V100, fp32, optimal batch size. 'other' target = audio (AudioSet).
evidence: "a simple method to increase the throughput of existing ViT models without needing to train" (Abstract); "In each block of a transformer, we merge tokens to reduce by r per layer." (Sec. 3); "we use a dot product similarity metric (e.g., cosine similarity) between the keys of each token to determine which contain similar information" (Sec. 3); "our method works with or without training" (Sec. 1)

name: ToMe for SD
backbones: Stable Diffusion v1.5 (U-Net with transformer blocks)
main_result: Stable Diffusion v1.5 512x512 (ImageNet-class prompts): FID 33.37 at 1.52 s/im (baseline 33.12 at 3.09 s/im), r = 60%, RTX 4090
notes: Tokens are latent patches inside the U-Net transformer blocks of Stable Diffusion. r% of the tokens are merged before the self-attention of the highest-resolution blocks (bipartite matching on the block input x, one dst token sampled per 2x2 region with randomness fixed across the batch) and unmerged right after by copying the merged token back to both positions, so every token is restored for the next module. A linear schedule over diffusion steps (more merging early) gives little gain. Time averaged over 2000 samples on one 4090; batch size not stated.
evidence: "our ToMe for Stable Diffusion can reduce the number of tokens in an existing Stable Diffusion model by up to 60% while still producing high quality images without any extra training" (Abstract); "Instead, we'd like to merge tokens, do some (now reduced) computation, and then unmerge them afterward so we don't lose any tokens." (Sec. 3.2); "Thus instead of removing a quantity of tokens r, we remove a percentage (r%) of all tokens." (Sec. 3.2); "we don't use proportional attention and use the input to the block x for similarly rather than attention keys k" (Sec. 3.2)

name: LTMP
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.6 at 3.0 GFLOPs after one fine-tuning epoch (baseline 79.9 at 4.6); 79.8 at 3.8 GFLOPs
notes: Between attention and MLP of every block: a learned threshold on the importance score (mean column attention, class attention also tested) decides pruning and a second learned threshold on ToMe's key similarity decides merging, so the number of removed tokens varies per image and per layer; merging dominates early layers, pruning late layers. Only two scalars per block are trained (straight-through estimator) for a single epoch with a FLOPs-target loss, backbone frozen. Inference needs batch size 1. FLOPs counted as multiply-adds. Mobile latency on a Google Pixel 7: DeiT-S 212 ms -> LTMP 107 ms at 2.3 GFLOPs (78.6%), ToMe 118 ms (76.9%). No GPU throughput.
evidence: "LTMP uses learned threshold masking modules that dynamically determine which tokens to merge and which to prune." (Abstract); "only tokens with an importance score above the threshold are kept" (Sec. 3.3.1); "We therefore only update the thresholds during training and keep all other trainable parameters fixed, allowing LTMP to converge within a single epoch." (Sec. 3.4.2); "Our learned thresholds approach requires a batch size of 1 during inference as each image is reduced differently." (Sec. 4.7)

name: STViT
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; Swin-T; Swin-S; Swin-B; LV-ViT-S; Video Swin-T; Video Swin-S
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.8 at 1.91 GFLOPs (16 semantic tokens; baseline 79.8 at 4.58)
notes: No per-token scoring: a semantic token generation module (two transformer layers at blocks 5-6 of DeiT) turns the 196 image tokens into 16 semantic tokens, initialised by intra/inter-window spatial pooling and refined by attention with the image tokens as keys and values; the image tokens are then discarded. STViT-R adds a recovery module and dumbbell units that restore the full-resolution map for COCO detection and segmentation (Swin). Throughput on a V100 with batch 128. Trained from scratch for 300 epochs.
evidence: "The semantic tokens represent cluster centers, and they are initialized by pooling image tokens in space and recovered by attention" (Abstract); "After the STGM, the image tokens X can be discarded, and only semantic tokens S with high-level semantic information are used in all the subsequent transformers" (3.1); "we design a STViT-R(ecover) network to restore the detailed spatial information based on the STViT, making it work for downstream tasks" (Abstract); "All the models are trained from scratch for 300 epochs" (4.1)

name: CF-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.8 at 1.8 GFLOPs (eta=0.5; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Coarse stage with 7x7 patches; if the confidence is below eta, the top-50% informative coarse patches (global class attention, EMA over encoders) are re-split 2x2 and a fine stage runs with feature reuse. Throughput on one A100 with batch 1024. Training follows the DeiT recipe (all patches fine-split for the first 200 epochs, then informative re-splitting); the paper does not use a pre-trained checkpoint, so training is taken as from scratch.
evidence: "At coarse inference stage, an input image is split into a small-length patch sequence for a computationally economical classification. If not well recognized, the informative patches are identified and further re-split in a fine-grained granularity" (Abstract); "it is natural to use the class attention a0k as a score to indicate if a token is informative" (Coarse Inference Stage); "if pcj >= eta, the inference will terminate" (Coarse Inference Stage); "All training settings of our CF-ViT, such as image processing, learning rate, etc, are to follow these of DeiT and LV-ViT" (Implementation Details)

name: DiffRate
main_result: DeiT-S off-the-shelf with learned rates: top-1 79.58 at 2.9 GFLOPs, 6744 img/s (baseline 79.82 at 4.6, 5039 img/s); with 30-epoch fine-tuning 79.83
notes: Per block, tokens are sorted by class attention; the N*alpha_p least important are pruned and the next N*(alpha_m - alpha_p) are merged into similar remaining tokens by cosine similarity. The pruning and merging rates per block are learned in 3 epochs with a differentiable discrete proxy (learnable probabilities over candidate rates, attention masking, FLOPs loss) while the backbone is frozen; 1,000 images suffice. The learned rates are then fixed, so every image keeps the same number of tokens (batchable). Reported off-the-shelf and with optional 30-epoch fine-tuning (dagger rows). Throughput on an A100 at batch 1024, fp16. Table 3 also gives latency and power on a Gemmini accelerator for a co-searched variant (batch not stated).
evidence: "by applying the learned layer-wise compression rates to an off-the-shelf ViT-H (MAE) model, we achieve a 40% FLOPs reduction and a 1.5x throughput improvement, with a minor accuracy drop of 0.16% on ImageNet without fine-tuning" (Abstract); "we set fc = fm o fp , meaning that tokens are first pruned and then merged" (Sec. 3); "we employ the class attention Ac in R1xN as the importance metric following EViT [21]" (Sec. 4.1); "We initialize the backbone models with pre-trained models and fix them to train the learnable probabilities in DDP" (Sec. 6.1); "We also fine-tune the model optionally for 30 epochs" (Sec. 6.1)

name: SparseViT
main_result: Swin-T (BEVDet, nuScenes): mAP 31.2 at 23.8 ms (baseline 31.2 at 36.4 ms, RTX A6000)
notes: Window-level activation pruning for Swin: windows are ranked by the L2 norm of their activations (score computed once per stage), only the top windows run MHSA, FFN and LN, and unselected windows keep duplicated features so the dense feature map survives (the paper calls this pruning; in the table vocabulary the windows halt). Per-layer sparsity (0-80%) is found by evolutionary search under a #MACs or measured-latency constraint after sparsity-aware adaptation, then the model is fine-tuned. Tasks: nuScenes 3D detection, COCO instance segmentation, Cityscapes semantic segmentation. Backbone latency on one RTX A6000; batch size not stated. No DeiT-S results; the code cell is the project page given in the paper.
evidence: "we define the importance of each window as its L2 activation magnitude" (3.2); "To mitigate information loss due to coarse-grained window pruning, we simply duplicate the features of the unselected windows" (3.2); "we make use of the evolutionary search to explore the best per-layer pruning ratios under a resource constraint" (1); "we finetune the model with the fixed sparsity configurations identified in the search process until convergence" (3.3)

name: STA
main_result: ViT-L (VideoMAE) Kinetics-400: top-1 85.0 at 308 GFLOPs per view (baseline 85.1 at 597 GFLOPs), STA64; ViT-H 86.1 at 611 GFLOPs (86.3 at 1192)
notes: Tokens are 3D tube embeddings (2x16x16 for ViT). A constant number r of tokens per frame is dropped at three stages with a decreasing schedule (e.g. 8x64, 8x32, 8x16 for ViT-L). Score: frame-to-frame affinity of attention keys accumulated along time as a Markov chain (temporal redundancy), reweighted by one minus the normalized L1 activation sum (semantic importance); the first frame is pruned with ToMe-style similarity. For VideoSwin the dropped positions are filled with the nearest kept tokens inside window attention. Throughput in clips/s on a V100 32G with batch 32.
evidence: "Based on the STA score, we are able to progressively prune the tokens without introducing any additional parameters or requiring further re-training." (Abstract); "For simplicity, we reduce a constant number of tokens in each frame to ensure parallel computing." (Sec. 3.2); "Note that we do not need to train a new projection head f because the self-attention provides the necessary functionality, and the key function fK extracts most relevant knowledge for affinity estimation" (Sec. 3.2); "Intuitively, through the summation of absolute activation values over channel dimension, a high absolute activation suggests a significant contribution to next layers." (Sec. 3.2)

name: HeatViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.34 at 2.64 GMACs (HeatViT-S2, 1.74x; baseline 79.8 at 4.6 GMACs; 8-bit)
notes: Token selector = multi-head token classifier (MLP per head, attention-based head weighting, Gumbel-softmax keep/prune mask with threshold 0.5) plus a token packager that averages non-informative tokens into one package token; the count varies per image. name: Token Merger

name: PaCa-ViT

main_result: PaCa-Small: ImageNet-1k top-1 83.08 at 5.5 GFLOPs (22.0M params; PVTv2-B2 82.0 at 3.9; DeiT-S 79.9 at 4.6)

The clusters are learned end-to-end" (Abstract); "a predefined number M of clusters (e.g., M = 100), we first compute the cluster assignment CN,M" (Sec. 3.2); "are trained for 300 epochs from scratch on 10 A100 GPUs" (Appendix)

notes: Analysis paper (ICCVW 2023), not a method. Ten token reduction methods (Top-K, EViT, DynamicViT, ATS, ToMe, K-Medoids, DPC-KNN, SiT, PatchMerger, Sinkhorn) plus three fixed radial baselines are inserted at blocks 4/7/10 of DeiT-T/S/B, fine-tuned (30 epochs on ImageNet) and compared on ImageNet, NABirds, COCO and NUS-WIDE at keep rates 25-90%. name: Tri-Level E-ViT

name: STTABT
notes: [core] Token pruning for ViTs and NLP Transformers judged from the abstract only; the full text could not be read. The OpenReview PDF is behind a browser challenge and there is no arXiv version, so schedule, training, backbones and all numbers are ?. Per the abstract, token importance is back-tracked through the attention from the outputs to the inputs; criterion is set to cls-attention (attention statistics) on that basis. The code URL is from the official README (repository linked to the OpenReview forum); the README mentions ViT and LV-ViT-S concrete-masking runs, GLUE tasks and DynamicViT comparison plots, which are not used here.

name: TAVT
main_result: ViT-B/16: CUB-200-2011 top-1 89.8 at 0.33x FLOPs, 50 ms GPU latency (ViT 90.6 at 1.00x, 134 ms); TAVTp 91.1 at 0.43x
notes: [core] Token pruning for fine-grained classification; published at DATE but contains no hardware design. Tokens are ranked by a significance score, the attention score aggregated over heads, and the top-k are kept. The fine-tuned ViT-B/16 is further fine-tuned with random progressive keep counts (n_{i+1} sampled in [(1-p) n_i, n_i], p=0.2), random layer skipping and sandwich-rule in-place distillation, so one model accepts any per-layer token configuration. A multi-objective evolutionary search with FLOPs as the constraint then picks per-layer token counts that are the same for every image (TAVTp: best accuracy, TAVTe: most efficient within 1% of ViT). Latency on one V100 GPU and an i9-9980XE CPU at batch size 8. FGVC only (CUB, Stanford Dogs, Stanford Cars, NABirds); no ImageNet or DeiT-S. Code not mentioned. Read the PDF in the official DATE 2023 proceedings archive.
evidence: "We identify the top-k attentive tokens based on the significance score and retain the highest value tokens based on the pruning scheme." (III.A); "we conduct a multi-objective evolutionary search to find the optimal token pruning scheme that maximizes accuracy and efficiency for the target computational budgets" (III.C); "Then we further fine-tuned the baseline ViT model on our token adaptive framework with a token drop rate set to 0.2." (IV. Experiments)

name: AiluRus
backbones: ViT-L; ViT-B (Segmenter); CAE ViT-L, ViT-B (Mask R-CNN)
main_result: Segmenter ViT-L ADE20K: mIoU 51.79 at 427.8 GFLOPs / 9.53 FPS (baseline 51.82 at 659.0 GFLOPs / 6.55 FPS), training-free
notes: At one intermediate layer a spatial-aware density peaks clustering (local density x distance indicator in feature space, restricted to lambda spatial neighbours) picks M cluster centers; the other tokens are averaged into their closest center, and representative tokens are re-weighted in attention by cluster size. The original resolution is recovered after the Segmenter decoder by copying each representative token to its region. M and the layer are fixed hyper-parameters. Main results plug into released checkpoints without training; the paper also uses AiluRus during fine-tuning (52.07 mIoU, 2.46x FPS, 52% less training time). FPS GPU and batch size not stated.
evidence: "With ρi and δi , we rank tokens according to ρi ∗ δi and select top M tokens as the cluster centers. The remaining tokens are assigned to the closest cluster centers, and tokens belonging to the same cluster centers are merged together as the representative token." (Sec. 3.2); "At the output stage, we restore the original resolution for prediction tasks by assigning the value of the representative token to its corresponding regions." (Sec. 1); "we adopt the benchmark of [15] and integrate our method into well-trained models without fine-tuning" (Sec. 1); "Moreover, we further apply AiluRus to accelerate the fine-tuning process." (Sec. 1)

name: Lite DETR
main_result: Lite-DINO Swin-T H3L1-(2+1)x3 COCO (36 epochs): AP 53.9 at 159 GFLOPs (DINO 54.1 at 243 GFLOPs)
notes: Not token reduction in the strict sense: no token is removed. The interleaved encoder updates the few high-level (low-resolution) tokens A times per block and the low-level tokens (about 75% of all tokens) only once at the end of each block, so most encoder layers process only 5-25% of the tokens as queries while all tokens stay as keys/values; the split is fixed by feature scale. Reducing encoder cost is the main purpose. Key-aware deformable attention compensates the lagged update. Detectors are trained with the baseline recipes. Only GFLOPs reported.
evidence: "FH is regarded as the primary feature and is updated more frequently, whereas FL is updated less frequently." (Sec. 3.3); "we stack the efficient encoder block for B times, where each block updates high-level features for A times but only updates low-level features once at the end of the block" (Sec. 3.3); "We train the model for 36/50 epochs according to the settings of different baselines" (Sec. 4.1)

name: SuperViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.0 at 2.3 GFLOPs (14x14 tokens, keep rate 0.5; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: One model is trained for four token grids (8x8 to 14x14, patches resized by bilinear interpolation into a shared embedding) times three keep rates {1.0, 0.7, 0.5}; tokens are dropped by class attention at blocks 4/7/10. At inference one (grid, keep rate) pair is picked for the available hardware budget, so each run is a fixed schedule. Throughput on one A100 with batch 512. Trained from scratch following the DeiT/LV-ViT recipes (4.1 days on 4 A100 for DeiT-S).
evidence: "the trained ViT model, termed super vision transformer (SuperViT), is empowered with the versatile ability to solve incoming patches of multiple sizes as well as preserve informative tokens with multiple keeping rates" (Abstract); "we directly preserve tokens with larger attention values in this paper" (3.2.2); "All the training strategies, such as data augmentation, regularization and optimizer, strictly follow the original settings of DeiT" (4.1)

name: AS-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.6 at 3.0 GFLOPs (f=0.65; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Class attention weighted by a per-token head importance (l2-norm of each head's context) scores tokens; three learnable thresholds before stages 2-4 keep tokens whose score exceeds the threshold, so the count varies per image. Thresholds are trained with a budget-aware FLOPs loss and distillation during 30-epoch fine-tuning. Throughput on one 2080Ti at batch 64; latency is single-image (6.56 ms vs 6.16 ms for DeiT-S). Code URL is from the arXiv comment, not the paper body. Not an RL method.
evidence: "learnable parameters are inserted as thresholds to distinguish informative tokens from unimportant ones" (Abstract); "We keep tokens with scores greater than the threshold" (3.3); "We finetune the pre-trained model by 30 epoch to obtain the compressed network" (4.1)

name: BAT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.6 at 3.0 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Token decoupling and merging at layers 4/7/10: class attention splits attentive and inattentive tokens; inattentive tokens are clustered by a simplified density-peak clustering and combined by attention-weighted sum; the top-K most similar attentive pairs are fused. No token is simply dropped. Trained from scratch for 300 epochs on 8 V100 with a cosine keep-rate schedule. Throughput on one V100 with batch 256. No code URL in the paper.
evidence: "According to the class token attention, we decouple the attentive and inattentive tokens. In addition to preserve the most discriminative local tokens, we merge similar inattentive tokens and match homogeneous attentive tokens to maximize the token diversity" (Abstract); "we select top-K most similar token pairs as homogeneous tokens. Finally, we combine each pair of tokens into a new token" (4.4); "all of our models are trained from scratch for 300 epochs on 8 NVIDIA V100" (5.1)

name: CTS
backbones: ViT-Ti/16; ViT-S/16; ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16; DeiT-B/16; BEiT-B/16; BEiT-L (Segmenter, UPerNet decoders)
main_result: Segmenter ViT-S/16 ADE20K: mIoU 45.1 at 162 im/s (baseline 45.0 at 122 im/s), 30% fewer tokens
notes: Reduction happens before the ViT. An EfficientNet-Lite0 policy network, trained separately on a binary label derived from the GT masks, predicts whether a 2x2 superpatch holds one class; the S highest-scoring superpatches are bilinearly downsampled to one patch and embedded as one token (M = N - 3S). Unsharing (reactivate): the shared token or its prediction is bilinearly upsampled to the 2x2 positions, before a CNN decoder or after a transformer decoder. The segmentation network is then trained with CTS using the original recipe. Throughput on A100 with batch 32. A per-image dynamic S is explored in Sec. 5.5 (+0.7 mIoU) but is not the main setting.
evidence: "each superpatch that can share a token according to policy P is bilinearly downsampled to the dimensions of a single patch, and linearly projected into a single token" (Sec. 3.2); "tu first unshares the shared tokens by bilinearly upsampling and rearranging them to produce L" (Sec. 3.2); "From the output of the network, the S highest-scoring superpatches are selected to share a token, to end up with M = N − 3S tokens that are processed by the transformer-based network." (Sec. 3.3); "Once the policy network is trained, we integrate it in the segmentation model and run the whole model end-to-end" (Sec. 4.3)

name: Token Pooling
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.6 at 2.6 GFLOPs with WK-Medoids (baseline DeiT-S retrained by the authors 81.2 at 4.6)
notes: K-Means or K-Medoids clustering of the tokens after each block, output = cluster centres; the optional weights and the centre initialisation use the significance score (total attention received by a token, PoWER-BERT style), so the criterion is feature similarity plus an attention statistic. The number of retained tokens per layer K is found offline with PoWER-BERT's soft-selection stage and is the same for every image. Main results fine-tune DeiT after inserting the pooling layers (training protocol in Sec. 5); Appendix E reports the no-fine-tuning case, where carrying the cluster counts into the softmax preserves the most accuracy. The abstract's 42% fewer computations refers to DeiT-Ti. GFLOPs include the clustering cost. No throughput or latency reported.
evidence: "It downsamples input tokens via clustering the tokens and returns the cluster centers (the average of the tokens in a cluster)." (Sec. 4); "A good choice of the weights is the significance scores (5), i.e., wi = si ." (Sec. 4); "we use the automatic search procedure proposed by Goyal et al. (2020) to determine K" (Appendix G); "(3) We further finetune the downsampling methods using K." (Sec. 5); "we evaluate the performance when we insert Token Pooling layers into a pre-trained model without finetuning" (Appendix E)

name: DynamicViT / DynamicCNN / DynamicSwin
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M; ConvNeXt-T/S/B; Swin-T/S/B
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.3 at 3.0 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Journal extension of DynamicViT (same predictor and ratio schedule). For hierarchical models the uninformative locations are not dropped but sent through a lightweight linear fast path instead of the FFN (asymmetric computation), which keeps the feature-map structure; that is the other part of operation. Dense tasks (ADE20k, COCO) use DynamicCNN on ConvNeXt, not DeiT. DeiT-S trained 30 epochs from pretrained; DynamicCNN 120 epochs. Throughput on one RTX 3090 with batch 128 (numbers differ slightly from the NeurIPS version).
evidence: "By applying lightweight fast paths to less informative features and expressive slow paths to important locations, we can maintain the complete structure of feature maps while significantly reducing the overall computations" (Abstract); "The training process includes training the prediction modules such that they can produce favorable decisions and fine-tuning the backbone to make it adapt to spatial sparsification" (Sec. 3.3)

name: TESTA
backbones: ViT-B/16 video encoder (BLIP initialization, divided space-time attention)
main_result: TESTA ViT-B/16 QuerYD paragraph-to-video retrieval (32 frames): R@1 77.0 at 420 GFLOPs (without aggregation 79.7 at 786 GFLOPs)
notes: Tokens are 16x16 patch tokens per frame plus pseudo frame tokens (mean of a frame's patches). Each video encoder block merges RT frames (temporal) and RS patches per frame (spatial) by bipartite matching on the cosine similarity of attention keys and averages the features; geometry-based (alternating) partition is the default, an importance-based partition (attention received) is a variant. Aggregation runs during pre-training (5M pairs) and fine-tuning. Efficiency is reported as GFLOPs and GPU memory only; the 1.7x in the abstract is FLOPs. Findings of EMNLP 2023, pages 932-947 (no arXiv id in the list).
evidence: "TESTA condenses video semantics by adaptively aggregating similar frames, as well as similar patches within each frame." (Abstract); "For each token in the set A, we find its most similar token from the set B, then merge them by averaging their features." (Sec. 3.2.2); "After each aggregation, TAM reduces RT frames while SAM reduce RS patches, where RT and RS are hyper-parameters to control the trade-offs between performance and efficiency." (Sec. 3.2); "We conduct our aggregation during both training and testing." (Sec. 3.2.2)

name: DToP
main_result: SETR ViT-B ADE20K: mIoU 47.0 at 80.6 GFLOPs (baseline 47.0 at 107.7 GFLOPs), p0 = 0.98
notes: Early exit of tokens. At fixed stages (after layers 6 and 8 for ViT-B, 8 and 16 for ViT-L) the inherent auxiliary segmentation head (ATM or FCN) grades every token; tokens whose max class probability is at least p0 get their prediction finalized from that head and leave the sequence (no reconstruction, the stage predictions are combined); the top-k (k = 5) most confident tokens of each present class are kept for context. The count varies per image, so average GFLOPs over the validation set are reported. Training variants: DToP@Direct (no training), DToP@Finetune (segmentation heads fine-tuned 40k iterations, adopted), DToP@Retrain (160k). Only FLOPs reported. No code link in the paper; the ALGM paper states that DToP did not release code.
evidence: "Easy tokens are halted and pruned early on in the ViT, while hard ones are kept to be computed in the following layers." (Sec. 1); "we prune the n-th token in Zlm if pm,n ⩾ p0 , otherwise we keep it. After propagating an image through the whole network, we combine the predicted token labels from each stage to form the final results." (Sec. 3.2); "DToP@Finetune means finetuning the segmentation heads for 40k iterations on the baseline model using DToP, and DToP@Retrain retraining the entire model using DToP for 160k iterations." (Sec. 4.3.1)

name: TPS
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-T; LV-ViT-S; PS-ViT; PVT-T; PVT-S; CvT-13; CvT-21
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.1 at 3.0 GFLOPs (dTPS, 100 fine-tuning epochs; baseline 79.8 at 4.6); eTPS 79.7 at 3.0 (30 epochs)
notes: Prune then squeeze: dTPS scores tokens with DynamicViT's learned head, eTPS with class-token attention; each pruned token is matched (cosine) to its nearest reserved host token and fused with similarity weights, keeping a constant shape. Fine-tuned 30 or 100 epochs from pre-trained weights. Throughput (RTX 2080Ti, batch 32) is shown only in figures; the text gives 1745 img/s for DeiT-S at the 35% FLOPs budget, not for the 3.0 GFLOPs row.
evidence: "Firstly, TPS adopts pruning to get the reserved and pruned subsets. Secondly, TPS squeezes the information of pruned tokens into partial reserved tokens via the unidirectional nearest-neighbor matching and similarity-based fusing steps" (Abstract); "dTPS adopts the learnable token score prediction head from dynamicViT ... eTPS utilizes the class token attention values to measure tokens' importance" (3.2); "we devise the token selection policy using the Top-k operation with a fixed given token reduction ratio" (3.2); "The model is initialized with pre-trained models' weights and fine-tuned with different token pruning locations and keeping ratios" (4)

name: PPT
backbones: DeiT-Ti; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-S; T2T-ViT; PS-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S fine-tuned 30 epochs: top-1 79.8 at 2.9 GFLOPs, 1448 img/s (baseline 79.8 at 4.6, 993 img/s); off-the-shelf 79.5 at 2.9 GFLOPs
notes: At layers 4, 7 and 10 of DeiT a fixed Top-K number of tokens is removed, but the policy is chosen per instance and layer: if the variance of the ATS-style importance scores (class attention times value norm) exceeds a threshold tau the inattentive tokens are pruned, otherwise similar tokens are pooled with ToMe's bipartite soft matching (size tracking and proportional attention). No trainable parameters; both off-the-shelf and 30-epoch fine-tuned results. Throughput on a single V100 at batch 256. Mirror code also at github.com/mindspore-lab/models.
evidence: "By heuristically integrating both token pruning and token pooling techniques in ViTs without additional trainable parameters" (Abstract); "we propose an adaptive strategy that takes into account both the instances and layers" (Sec. 3.4); "we return to the traditional Top-K selection policy for more controllable compression ratio" (Sec. 3.2); "we report the performance of our method in terms of both off-the-shelf and fine-tuned" (Sec. 4)

name: IdleViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.6 at 3.1 GMACs, 3361.3 img/s (k=0.7; baseline 79.8 at 4.6, 2476.8 img/s)
notes: In each layer the top-K image tokens by [CLS] attention go through MHSA and FFN; the other tokens stay idle and are copied to the layer output, so they can be selected again in later layers (keep ratios 1, k, k^2, k^3 over four stages). 'halt' is the closest value: idle tokens skip a layer but are not stopped for good. A token cut loss (normalized graph cut on the attention map) is used only during fine-tuning. Fine-tuned 30 epochs from pre-trained weights with logit and feature distillation. Speed on one V100, batch 128. Not RL.
evidence: "in each layer, IdleViT selects a subset of the image tokens to participate in computations while keeping the rest of the tokens idle and directly passing them to this layer’s output" (Abstract); "image tokens with top-K attention scores towards the [CLS] token are selected and straightforwardly named the Selected tokens" (3.2); "All the models are finetuned for only 30 epochs" (4.1)

name: MG-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.8 at 2.0 GFLOPs (eps=0.49; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Two stages: 7x7 tokens first; if the top softmax score is below eps, head and middle patches (by EMA global class attention) are re-split 3x3 and 2x2 with feature reuse. The slimming module keeps positive tokens, merges boundary tokens by bipartite cosine matching on value vectors, and fuses negative tokens into one. Hierarchical variant on PVT-S for COCO and ADE20K. Trained 300 epochs following the DeiT and LV-ViT recipes; no checkpoint is mentioned, so training is taken as from scratch. Throughput on RTX 3090 (batch not stated). No code URL. Not RL.
evidence: "In single-granularity inference stage, an input image is split into a small number of patches for simple inference" (Abstract); "Boundary and negative tokens are respectively merged by different rules to reduce their numbers" (Introduction); "use AdamW optimizer to train all models for 300 epochs" (Appendix 7.2)

name: SegViT v2 (Shrunk++)
backbones: ViT-B; ViT-L; BEiTv2-B; BEiTv2-L (ATM decoder); Swin-T
main_result: BEiTv2-L 640x640 ADE20K: mIoU 55.7 (ss) / 57.0 (ms) at 308.8 GFLOPs / 9.38 FPS (SegViT 58.0 / 58.2 at 637.9 GFLOPs / 6.25 FPS)
notes: Token reduction is one part of the paper (the other parts are the ATM decoder and continual learning). Query downsampling (QD) keeps one token of every 2 x 2 window as queries while all tokens stay as keys/values; in Shrunk++ (EQD) tokens that an MLP edge head marks as edge (threshold tau = 0.7, trained with edges from the GT masks) are also kept, so the count varies per image. Query upsampling (QU) recovers the full-resolution tokens by cross-attention with stored high-resolution queries. The segmentation network is trained 160k/80k iterations from pre-trained backbones. FPS on one A100; batch size not stated.
evidence: "This method employs query-based down-sampling (QD) to prune the input token sequence Fi and uses query up-sampling (QU) to retrieve the discarded tokens, ensuring preservation of fine-detail features vital for semantic segmentation." (Sec. 3.2); "a viable strategy is to selectively reduce the number of query tokens while preserving the key and value tokens" (Sec. 3.2); "To determine the confidence level of a token belonging to an edge, we apply a threshold τ . In our implementation, we set τ to 0.7." (Sec. 3.2); "The batch size is set to 16 for all datasets with a total iteration of 160k, 80k, and 80k" (Sec. 4.1)

name: Focus-DETR
backbones: ResNet-50; ResNet-101; Swin-T (DINO / Deformable DETR encoder)
main_result: ResNet-50 DINO COCO: AP 50.4 at 154 GFLOPs / 20.0 FPS (DINO 50.9 at 279 GFLOPs / 14.2 FPS), keep ratio 0.3
notes: Encoder tokens of DINO / Deformable DETR. A Foreground Token Selector (shared MLP with top-down score modulation across scales, trained with focal loss against GT boxes) picks foreground queries; the paper says background queries are abandoned, but in Algorithm 1 all tokens stay as keys/values and only foreground tokens are updated, so the operation is halt. A multi-category score picks a few fine-grained object tokens for an extra self-attention (dual attention). Cascade: the number of foreground tokens is reduced layer by layer. The whole detector is trained for 36 epochs. FPS on V100; batch size not stated. The abstract links a torch and a mindspore version but the URLs are not in the PDF text.
evidence: "Foreground Token Selector (FTS) aims to abandon background tokens based on top-down score modulations across multi-scale features. We assign {1,0} labels to all tokens from the backbone with reference to the ground truth and predict the foreground probability." (Sec. 1); "we design the cascade structure for the encoder to reduce the number of foreground tokens layer by layer" (Sec. 4.4); "update Tf′ in Ta according to If" (Algorithm 1); "Like DETR-like detectors, our model is trained in an end-to-end manner" (Sec. 3.5)

name: ReViT
backbones: DeiT-S; LV-ViT-S; MotionFormer ViT-B; MotionFormer ViT-L
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 -0.1 at 50% acceleration (Intro; numbers only in Fig. 5 and Fig. 8)
notes: A Token-Length Assigner (small EfficientNet-B0) predicts per image which of 14x14, 10x10 or 7x7 token grids to use; the Resizable-ViT handles all lengths with token-length-aware LayerNorm and self-distillation. DeiT-S ImageNet results appear only as accuracy-throughput plots (RTX 3090, batch 32), no table, so top-1, GFLOPs and throughput cannot be copied. No code URL. ECML PKDD 2023 per arXiv comment.
evidence: "we introduce a method for adaptively assigning token length for each image at test time to accelerate inference speed" (Abstract); "we train a lightweight Token-Length Assigner (TLA) that allocates the optimal token length for each image during inference" (Abstract); "The throughput is measured on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU with batch size fixed to 32" (Fig. 5); "Our proposed ReViT is almost a cheap as training the baseline DeiT-S" (Fig. 7)

name: MonoATT
main_result: GUPNet (DLA34) + MonoATT: KITTI test car AP3D (moderate) 17.37 at 56 ms (GUPNet 14.20 at 40 ms)
notes: [application] Monocular 3D detection on KITTI with token clustering inside a transformer on top of a CNN detector. Tokens are the pixels of a DLA34 feature map; a scoring network (depth prior from the camera model plus a learned semantic keypoint heatmap, focal-loss supervised) picks n_l cluster centers per stage, other tokens join the nearest center by feature distance minus pixel distance, and are merged by attention-weighted averaging. Multi-stage feature reconstruction copies merged features back to a full feature map for the detection head. The number of centers per stage is preset. The paper does not say whether the detector starts from pre-trained weights, so training is ?. Time per image is given without batch size or GPU in the text. No code link ("will be released").
evidence: "we first use prior knowledge to design a scoring network for selecting the most important areas of the image, and then propose a token clustering and merging network with an attention mechanism to gradually merge tokens around the selected areas in multiple stages" (Abstract); "The detection network is supervised by LCCE and can be trained jointly with other Mono3D branches" (3.1); "In the upsampling process, we use the record to copy the merged token features to the corresponding upsampled tokens" (3.3)

name: STP + MTA
main_result: ViT-B + UNETR: BraTS DSC 75.79 at 7.79 img/s encoder throughput (r=0.75; UNETR 75.44 at 4.85)
notes: [application] 3D medical image segmentation (BTCV CT, MSD BraTS MRI) with a ViT-B encoder and UNETR decoder. Soft-topK Token Pruning: an MLP sub-network scores tokens and keeps the top K = (1 - r) n at blocks 3, 6 and 9 (straight-through Gumbel top-K in training, plain top-K at inference). Multi-layer Token Assembly then puts the pruned intermediate tokens (with block tokens) back with the output tokens and runs Transformer blocks before the decoder. Trained with the segmentation loss only; whether the ViT-B starts from pre-trained weights is not said, so training is '?'. Throughput on one A100 at batch size 1; training throughput also rises (up to 120%). Read arXiv v1 (12 pages, the IPMI text was not compared).
evidence: "STP predicts token importance scores with a lightweight sub-network and samples the topK tokens" (Abstract); "In token completion, MTA restores a full token sequence by assembling both sparse output tokens and pruned multi-layer intermediate ones." (Abstract); "Three STP modules are inserted after the 3rd, 6th, and 9th Transformer blocks in ViT-B." (3.2)

name: vid-TLDR
main_result: UMT-B MSRVTT text-video retrieval: R@1 50.8 at 178.0 GFLOPs (baseline 50.0 at 303.3 GFLOPs)
notes: Tokens are the tube embeddings of the video encoder (UMT). ToMe bipartite soft matching in the first four layers. Saliency is the normalized negative entropy (sharpness) of each token's attention row, no class token needed; tokens below the mean saliency get mass 0 in the weighted average, so background tokens are effectively dropped (the paper calls it a combination of merging and pruning). A fixed number of tokens is merged per video (per-dataset numbers in the supplement). Only FLOPs reported.
evidence: "we propose training-free token merging for lightweight video Transformer (vid-TLDR) that aims to enhance the efficiency of video Transformers by merging the background tokens without additional training" (Abstract); "we devise a sharpness function S to capture the saliency of tokens with entropy" (Sec. 3.1); "Although the same number of tokens are merged in each video, we dynamically adjust the influence of uninformative tokens by suppressing the mess" (Sec. 3.2)

backbones: DeiT-III ViT-B; OpenCLIP ViT-B/16; DINOv2 ViT-L/14; DINOv2 ViT-g/14
notes: Analysis paper (ICLR 2024), not a token reduction method.
