Supervised (DeiT-III), text-supervised (OpenCLIP) and self-supervised (DINOv2) ViTs produce a few (about 2%) high-norm outlier tokens (about 10x norm) from the middle layers of large, long-trained models; they sit on patches redundant with their neighbours (background), carry little local information but strong global information, i.e. the model reuses them as scratch space. Adding learnable register tokens removes the artifacts, keeps linear-probe accuracy, and improves dense tasks (ADE20k, NYUd) and object discovery (LOST). Relevant to token reduction because token norm and attention maps are used as importance scores. No code URL of its own in the paper (official DeiT, OpenCLIP and DINOv2 repositories are cited for training).
evidence: "The artifacts correspond to high-norm tokens appearing during inference primarily in low-informative background areas of images, that are repurposed for internal computations" (Abstract); "We observe that they are tokens with roughly 10x higher norm at the output and correspond to a small fraction of the total sequence (around 2%)" (1); "the model learns to recognize patches containing little useful information, and recycle the corresponding tokens to aggregate global image information while discarding spatial information" (1); "we observe that the outlier tokens disappear from the sequence entirely. As a result, the performance of the models increases in dense prediction tasks" (1)

name: Bootstrapped SparseFormer
backbones: AugReg ViT-B/16-224; AugReg ViT-L/16-224; AugReg ViT-L/16-384; CLIP ViT-B/16; CLIP ViT-L/14; CLIP ViT-L/14-336
main_result: AugReg ViT-B/16 to SF-B with 49 tokens: top-1 82.5 at 3.8 GFLOPs, 3001 img/s (ViT-B/16 84.6 at 17.5 GFLOPs, 1126 img/s)
notes: [core] Converts a pre-trained ViT into a SparseFormer with 1/4 of its tokens (49 by default) and reports ImageNet accuracy and throughput. The cortex transformer inherits the ViT blocks (first 1/3 dropped, middle blocks tuned, last 1/3 frozen), a new focusing transformer is trained from random, and the final representation is aligned to the original ViT on ImageNet-1k images without labels. Also CLIP zero-shot and retrieval, MLLM (ScienceQA) and ADE20K segmentation. Throughput on one A5000, fp16, batch 128. Bootstrapping from ViT-L/16 takes 6 hours on 8 A5000.
evidence: "we only need to train the SparseFormer-specific lightweight focusing transformer to adjust token RoIs and fine-tune a few early pre-trained blocks to align the final token representation" (Abstract); "We typically set the number of sparse latent tokens in SparseFormers to 1/4 those in vision transformers" (Figure 2)

name: SparseFormer
main_result: SparseFormer-T: top-1 81.0 at 2.0 GFLOPs, 1270 img/s (Swin-T 81.3 at 4.5 GFLOPs, 726 img/s)
notes: [core] New architecture that represents an image by a small fixed set of latent tokens (49 to 81) with learnable RoIs instead of dense patches. A light focusing transformer adjusts token RoIs and samples features by bilinear interpolation from an early conv feature map; a standard cortex transformer then runs on the latent tokens only. Token count is fixed per variant. Trained from scratch on ImageNet-1k; throughput on one V100 (batch size not in the text). Also Kinetics-400. Not token reduction in a pre-trained ViT. Read the arXiv v1 (only version).
evidence: "SparseFormer learns to represent images using a highly limited number of tokens (down to 49) in the latent space with sparse feature sampling procedure instead of processing dense units in the original pixel space" (Abstract); "SparseFormer uses a learnable linear layer to generate a set of sampling offsets for a token conditionally on its embedding t" (3.1); "SparseFormer, as a new visual architecture, learns to represent an image with sparse tokens from scratch" (3. SparseFormer)

name: ATC
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; ViT-B; ViT-L; ViT-H (MAE); Stable Diffusion v1.5; ViT-Adapter-T; ViT-Adapter-S
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.82 at keep rate 70% (ATC-average, fine-tuned; baseline 79.85; FLOPs not reported); ViT-L MAE off-the-shelf: top-1 84.8 (constant t=8; ToMe 84.2; baseline 85.9)
notes: ToMe with the bipartite matching replaced by agglomerative (bottom-up hierarchical) clustering on the cosine distance of keys, with single, average or complete linkage; cluster members are averaged with size weighting and proportional attention; parameter-free. Reported off-the-shelf and after 30-epoch fine-tuning on DeiT (blocks 4/7/10, keep rates 25-90%), MAE ViT-B/L/H (per-block constant or linear schedule), Stable Diffusion (FID) and COCO ViT-Adapter. Largest gains at keep rates 25-50%; off-the-shelf DeiT-S collapses at r=25% (24.27). FLOPs are not reported. Throughput is only plotted (Fig. 11, A40 GPU, batch sizes 1 to 1024) and is below ToMe at large batch because the clustering runs on the CPU (scikit-learn). The code cell is the project page.
evidence: "ATC merges clusters through bottom-up hierarchical clustering, without the introduction of extra learnable parameters" (Abstract); "we use the cosine distance as our distance metric D(.) and the keys from the self-attention module as token features" (3.2); "In this paper we consider the static reduction scenario" (3.2); "we report both off-the-shelf results, where ATC is inserted into the pre-trained model and evaluated without any fine-tuning, and results after fine-tuning" (4)

name: Salience DETR
main_result: ResNet-50 COCO (12 epochs): AP 49.2 at 201 GFLOPs (DINO 49.0 at 291 GFLOPs)
notes: Encoder tokens of a multi-scale DETR. A salience predictor, supervised by a scale-independent target built from GT boxes (focal loss), scores each token; per encoder layer and per feature level only the top v_t * w_l tokens are updated, the others are kept unchanged (Focus-DETR style). Also adds background embedding, cross-level token fusion and NMS on two-stage queries. The whole detector is trained (12 epochs on COCO). Inference time per image in Table 10 (CSD); GPU and batch size not stated for it. The filtering ratio values are not in the main text.
evidence: "For the t-th encoder layer and l-th feature level, only the top vt wl queries are filtered for attention encoding while others are kept unchanged" (Sec. 3.2); "we construct a scale-independent salience as supervision targets to overcome the scale bias" (Sec. 3.1); "For COCO 2017, we report the results of 12 epochs." (Sec. 4.1)

name: LF-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.8 at 1.7 GFLOPs (m=5, eta=0.47; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Localization stage on a 112x112 downsampled image (7x7 tokens); if the confidence is below eta, NGCA (sliding-window sum of EMA class attention) picks an m x m region, and the top alpha*m^2 tokens of that region from the full-resolution image go to the focus stage, while other tokens are reused from the localization stage. Trained 350 epochs with the DeiT recipe; no pre-trained checkpoint is mentioned, so training is taken as from scratch. Throughput on one A100, batch 1024. Not RL.
evidence: "In the Localization phase, a reduced-resolution image is processed; if a definitive prediction remains elusive, our pioneering Neighborhood Global Class Attention (NGCA) mechanism is triggered" (Abstract); "we select the highest GCA α × m2 tokens from the localized class-discriminative regions in the original image as the input of the focus stage" (Focus Inference Stage); "We train LF-ViT for a total of 350 epochs" (Implementation Details)

name: TSMVT
main_result: 30% fewer tokens with higher precision on marine species classification (numbers not in the abstract)
notes: [application] Underwater fine-grained classification for autonomous underwater vehicles. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. A dynamic token filtering mechanism keeps important tokens, merges low-information tokens and discards background tokens; a multihead attention weighting token-selective (MAWTS) module re-weights attention. The scoring rule, schedule, backbone and training are not described. Four marine and three terrestrial datasets.
evidence: "we propose a dynamic token filtering mechanism that effectively retains important tokens, merges low-information tokens, and discards irrelevant background tokens" (Abstract); "With a 30% reduction in tokens, TSMVT achieves superior precision in classifying marine species" (Abstract)

name: ToCom
main_result: DeiT-B on VTAB-1k: a model fine-tuned without ToMe (source r=0) and run with ToMe r=16 (1.9x inference speedup) gains +2.1/+3.6/+1.2 average accuracy on the Natural/Specialized/Structured groups when ToCom is plugged in
notes: Not a new reduction rule: the compression is ToMe (fixed r per layer, key similarity, bipartite soft matching) or EViT. ToCom is a set of LoRA plugins (16 groups, 1.2M params for DeiT-B, h=2 on Wq/Wv) trained once on ImageNet for 10 epochs by self-distillation between random source/target compression degrees with the whole backbone frozen; at inference the plugins are added or subtracted to any downstream fine-tuned model so that it can run at a different r without re-tuning. Evaluated on CIFAR100, 4 FGVC datasets and VTAB-1k; DeiT-S only on VTAB-1k (Table 9), no ImageNet-1k accuracy. Throughput of DeiT-B versus r in Fig. 3 (batch 256 inference, GPU not stated); training on 8xV100.
evidence: "we additionally perform a fast parameter-efficient self-distillation stage on the pre-trained models to obtain a small plugin, called Token Compensator (ToCom), which describes the gap between models across different compression degrees" (Abstract); "It leverages the keys of patch tokens to evaluate their similarity, and merges r similar ones with Bipartite Soft Matching." (Sec. 3.1); "we freeze all pre-trained parameters including the classification heads, and only update the parameter-efficient ToCom" (Sec. 4.2)

name: Segformer++
main_result: Segformer-B5 Cityscapes inference: mIoU 82.31 at 23.68 FPS (baseline 82.39 at 14.75 FPS), Segformer++HQ, A100 batch 8
notes: Hierarchical Segformer (MiT), not a plain ViT. In every attention layer ToMe-style bipartite merging (averaging) is applied to the queries (stages 3-4, rate 0.8 / 0.9) and to the spatially reduced keys/values (stages 1-2, rate 0.6 / 0.9), and tokens are unmerged by copying after attention (ToMeSD style). Rates per stage were chosen by experiments (HQ and fast variants), same for every image. Inference-only use (B2 official weights; B5 weights trained by the authors) and training with merging (Table III) are both reported. FPS on one A100 with batch 8 (B5) or 16 (B2). The code URL is a project page.
evidence: "Our architecture is identical to the original Segformer architecture, except for the attention where we apply token merging after the Spatial Reduction mechanism and unmerge the tokens after the attention." (Sec. III-C); "Merging is computed via averaging and unmerging is done by copying a token to all positions that were merged into it." (Sec. III-B); "We conduct multiple experiments to find the optimal rates for each stage." (Sec. III-C); "Our merging strategies offer the advantage of being applicable without requiring model re-training." (Sec. IV-B)

name: ToFu
main_result: ViT-B (MAE, off-the-shelf, r=8): top-1 83.22 at 13.12 GFLOPs, 413.9 im/s with MLERP (ToMe 82.86 at 413.7 im/s; full model 83.74 at 17.58 GFLOPs, 323.6 im/s)
notes: Same bipartite soft matching as ToMe (key similarity, fixed r per layer), but in layers l < d (d=6) the matched source tokens are simply dropped ('pruned merging', faster) and in later layers they are averaged with norm-preserving MLERP (normalised mean scaled by the max norm); choice motivated by the measured functional linearity of the MLPs. Evaluated off-the-shelf (the paper says training is optional but reports none). DeiT-S itself is not run: Table 4 lists ToFu on AugReg ViT-S r=13 at 79.6% / 2.7 GFLOPs / 1561 img/s next to ToMe's DeiT-S numbers. Throughput on V100, fp32. Also applied to Stable Diffusion (FID, LPIPS, time per image). No code URL in the paper.
evidence: "ToFu is versatile, applicable to ViTs with or without additional training." (Abstract); "Central to its operation is the Bipartite Soft Matching (BSM) algorithm [3], which discerns the top r token pairs based on their mutual similarity." (Sec. 3); "early layers use pruned merging, while later layers transition to average (or MLERP) merging" (Fig. 2 caption); "For classification, the settings align with ToMe [3], with token numbers linearly decaying by factor r." (Sec. 4)

name: LookupViT
backbones: ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16 (LookupViT versions); ViViT B/16 (LookupViViT); LookupViT encoder with a text decoder for COCO captioning
main_result: LookupViT-B/16 (5x5 compressed tokens): ImageNet-1k top-1 79.1 at 16.5 GFLOPs (ViT-B/16 78.6 at 35.1, both trained from scratch)
notes: Architecture-type method. The input tokens are bilinearly resized to a fixed grid of M compressed tokens (3x3 to 10x10). Heavy self-attention and the full MLP run only on the M compressed tokens, while the N lookup tokens are updated by a cross-attention that reuses the same attention weights and a small MLP. M is a user choice, the same for every image, and can be changed at inference when trained with random M. Trained from scratch on ImageNet-1k, or pre-trained on ImageNet-21k and fine-tuned. The paper's GFLOPs for ViT-B/16 at 224 is 35.1. No throughput or latency. No code link in the paper (JAX, Big Vision).
evidence: "A fixed number of tokens M (≪ N ), which we name as the compressed tokens are sampled from the input tokens, using bilinear interpolation." (Sec. 3.1); "Compressed tokens use cross-attention to “look" at the original tokens (termed lookup tokens) and gather relevant information." (Sec. 3.1); "We evaluate LookupViT on image classification while – (a) training from scratch on ImageNet-1k [11], and (b) finetuning on ImageNet-1k from a ImageNet-21k pre-trained model." (Sec. 4)

name: DTEM
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; MAE-B; MAE-L; LV-ViT-S; DeiT-T; ViT-S (AugReg, 384px); GIT-B/L (captioning); Segmenter-S (ADE20K)
main_result: DeiT-S end-to-end (30 epochs): top-1 79.85 at 2.9 GFLOPs, 1991 im/s (baseline 79.83 at 4.64, 1390 im/s); modular with frozen backbone 79.44 at 2.91 GFLOPs, 1991 im/s
notes: A lightweight per-block linear embedding (output dim 64, <1% of parameters), decoupled from the ViT features, produces the similarity used by ToMe-style bipartite matching; it is trained through a continuous relaxation (soft top-k grouping and soft merging) with the task loss. 'mixed' here means two trained variants, not training-free: modular (only the embedding trained, backbone frozen = light) or end-to-end (backbone fine-tuned with alternating updates). Inference uses hard BSM with a fixed r per block and proportional attention; a model trained at r=16 generalises to smaller r. Throughput on one RTX 3090, batch 128, fp32.
evidence: "Our method introduces a lightweight embedding module decoupled from the ViT forward pass to extract dedicated features for token merging" (Abstract); "trained either modularly by learning only the decoupled embeddings or end-to-end by fine-tuning" (Abstract); "we employ a uniform reduction strategy, where the reduction rate r represents the number of tokens removed in each transformer block" (Sec. 4.1); "we employ BSM to speed up the inference" (Sec. 3.4)

name: MCTF
main_result: DeiT-S fine-tuned 30 epochs with r=16: top-1 80.1 at 2.6 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6); without training 79.2 at 2.6 GFLOPs
notes: Bidirectional bipartite soft matching with an attraction score that multiplies three criteria: cosine similarity, informativeness (inverse of the mean attention each token receives, taken from the one-step-ahead attention of the next layer and then aggregated for the fused tokens) and inverse token size; fused by attention- and size-weighted average; proportional attention. A fixed r=16 tokens per layer. Fine-tuned 30 epochs with a token-reduction-consistency loss between r and a random r' (no mixup); Table 3 and Appendix Table D give results without any training (the model finetuned at r=16 is also evaluated at other r). Only FLOPs reported, no throughput or latency.
evidence: "a Multi-criteria Token Fusion (MCTF), that gradually fuses the tokens based on multi-criteria (i.e., similarity, informativeness, and size of fused tokens)" (Abstract); "we measure the averaged attention scores a in [0, 1]^N in the self-attention layer, which indicates the impact of each token on others" (Sec. 3.2); "MCTF is applicable with pre-trained ViTs without any additional training since MCTF does not require any learnable parameters" (Sec. 4.1); "we finetune the model with the pre-trained weights for 30 epochs" (Appendix A)

name: DoViT
backbones: ViT-S; ViT-B; ViT-L; DeiT-S; DeiT-B (SETR, Segmenter)
main_result: SETR ViT-B Cityscapes: mIoU 76.40 at 330.09 GFLOPs (baseline 76.59 at 703.28), xi = 0.985
notes: Early exit of tokens. After decision layers (3, 6, 9 for S/B; 6, 12, 18 for L) a one-layer auxiliary segmentation head gives each token a confidence (max class probability); tokens above threshold xi stop and skip all later self-attention, the rest continue, so the count varies per image. The mean of the stopped tokens is added to the class token (fuse). A token reconstruction module puts the stopped tokens back in their positions for the auxiliary heads and the decoder. The segmentation network is trained with the official SETR/Segmenter recipes plus self-distillation from the dense ViT. Throughput and FPS on one V100 (512 x 512 crops); batch size not stated.
evidence: "The keeping tokens will involve in the next self-attention layers while the stopping tokens will be prevented from the self-attention and directly passed to the decoder via a short path." (Sec. 1); "The keep or stop of each token is determined by the semantic prediction confidence provided by the auxiliary heads." (Sec. 1); "we merge them as one representative token and aggregate it with the class token before calculating self-attention in the next block" (Sec. 3.3); "we employ a self-distillation framework to train the DoViT-based segmentation network with the corresponding ViT-based network as a teacher" (Sec. 3.4)

name: METR
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; MAE ViT-B; MAE ViT-L
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.64 at 3.0 GFLOPs (METR+EViT, 30-epoch fine-tuning; EViT 79.32; baseline 79.82 at 4.6)
notes: Adds early-exit heads with self-distillation in every reduction block during training so that early [CLS] attention becomes a reliable token score; heads are removed after training. Built on EViT (keep ratio at blocks 4, 7, 10, inattentive tokens fused into one) or on DiffRate (prune+merge with learned rates). Also reports from-scratch (79.76) and 100-epoch (80.09) settings for DeiT-S at 3.0 GFLOPs. Throughput 3582 img/s is from Table 1 (keep ratio 0.7, 3.0 GFLOPs, RTX 4090, batch 512), the same reduction setting. No code URL in the paper.
evidence: "By injecting early task pressure via multi-exit loss, the [CLS] token is spurred to collect task-related information in even early blocks, thus bolstering the credibility of [CLS] attention as a token-scoring metric" (Abstract); "reduce the number of tokens according to the specified keep ratio (e.g. 30% of the tokens are reduced when keep ratio set to 0.7) in the 4-th, 7-th, and 10-th blocks, and fuse the unimportant tokens into one additional token" (Sec. 4); "for those without special notation we start from supervised checkpoints and fine-tune for 30 epochs" (Table 5)

name: SViT
main_result: DeiT-S ViT-Adapter Mask R-CNN COCO: box AP 48.2 / mask AP 42.5 at 15.75 FPS (dense 48.5 / 42.8 at 11.70 FPS), A100 batch 1
notes: Pruned tokens are preserved in the feature map (used by the detection head) and can be reactivated by the gating MLP of any later layer. A 2-layer MLP with Gumbel softmax before each of blocks 4-12 decides per token; target keep ratios 70/49/34.3% are enforced by a loss averaged over the batch, so the count varies per image (dynamic rate). Detector fine-tuned 6 (tiny) / 4 (small) epochs after dense training. ImageNet numbers (Table 6) after a 30-epoch fine-tune from DeiT-S; throughput 2246 vs 1524 img/s on A100 with batch 512. Detection FPS on A100 with batch 1 (nested tensors not used for detection).
evidence: "tokens should not be completely pruned and discarded, but rather preserved in the feature maps for later use. (ii) reactivating previously pruned tokens can further enhance model performance. (iii) a dynamic pruning rate based on images is better than a fixed pruning rate. (iv) a lightweight, 2-layer MLP can effectively prune tokens" (Abstract); "For controlling the number of pruned tokens, similar to [32], we use a dynamic pruning ratio loss during training" (Sec. 3.3); "Then we finetune each sparse model for 6 and 4 epochs for tiny and small models, respectively" (Sec. 4)

name: LTRP
backbones: MAE ViT-B; MAE ViT-L; MAE ViT-H (ranking model ViT-S or ViT-T)
main_result: ViT-B: top-1 83.1 at 13.1 GFLOPs (keep ratio 0.75, ViT-T ranking model; baseline 83.3 at 17.6)
notes: Input-level patch selection before the backbone. A separate ranking model learns with ListMLE to rank patches by self-supervised pseudo scores (change of the MAE reconstruction when a visible patch is removed); top-k patches plus a few DPC-KNN cluster representatives from homogeneous regions are kept at a fixed keep ratio. The classifier is initialized from the MAE encoder and trained on the kept patches. GPU/CPU throughput reported (3090 server; batch size not stated). No DeiT-S ImageNet-1k result (ViT-S only on ImageNet-100). Not RL.
evidence: "inferring the semantic density score of each patch by quantifying variation between reconstructions with and without this patch, and learning to rank the patches with the pseudo score" (Abstract); "Top-k patches are selected using the trained ranking model and fed into downstream tasks" (Fig. 2); "They are both initialized from the MAE encoder" (Sec. 4.1)

name: PaPr
backbones: ViT-S/16; ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16; ViT-H/16 (AugReg, MAE); ViT-Medium-GAP; DeiT-S; ConvNeXt-B; ConvNeXt-L; Swin-B; Swin-L; ViT-B/L MAE (video)
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.2 at 2.7 GFLOPs (z=0.55, trained; baseline 79.8 at 4.6); training-free ViT-B/16 AugReg: 82.11 at 8.98 GFLOPs (baseline 84.59 at 17.59)
notes: A pre-trained lightweight ConvNet (MobileOne-S0) with its FC weights set uniform gives a patch significance map (channel mean of the last conv features, upsampled); the top-z% patches are kept in one step right after patch embedding (criterion 'other' = external ConvNet saliency, no training of the selector). Also applied to ConvNeXt and Swin (pixel operators run only on kept patches, rest zero-padded) and to video (Kinetics-400, ViT-MAE). The DeiT-S row comes from the training comparison (Table 4: PaPr trained, 1.6x training speed); all other rows are training-free. Throughput on one RTX A5000, batch size not stated.
evidence: "we introduce PaPr, a method for substantially pruning redundant patches with minimal accuracy loss using lightweight ConvNets across a variety of deep learning architectures, including ViTs, ConvNets, and hybrid transformers, without any re-training" (Abstract); "we identify the indices corresponding to the top-z% patches as per M, facilitating the retention of only the most salient patches in F" (3.2); "our approach seeks to eliminate redundant tokens early in the processing pipeline, immediately following initial patch extraction" (3.3); "We report training-free results of PaPr, unless otherwise specified" (4.1)

name: SlowFormer
backbones: ViT-Ti; ViT-S; ViT-B (with A-ViT, ATS, AdaViT)
main_result: A-ViT ViT-S ImageNet: a universal 64x64 patch (8% of the image) raises GFLOPs from 3.7 to 4.6 (Attack Success 99%, top-1 78.8% to 2.3%); ATS ViT-S 3.1 to 4.0 GFLOPs (60%); AdaViT ViT-S 2.25 to 3.2 (40%)
notes: Analysis (attack) paper, not a reduction method. One universal adversarial patch, optimized on the ImageNet train set, pushes input-adaptive token reduction (A-ViT, ATS, AdaViT) back toward full compute on any image; on A-ViT it undoes 99 to 100% of the FLOPs savings, and adversarial training reduces part of the effect. Only FLOPs are reported, as a proxy for energy.
evidence: "We show that such models can be vulnerable to a universal adversarial patch attack, where the attacker optimizes for a patch that when pasted on any image, can increase the compute and power consumption of the model." (Abstract); "Our attack has an Attack Success of 60% on ATS and 40% on AdaViT with ViT-Small." (Sec. 5.1); "we do not experiment with real hardware to measure the power consumption" (Sec. 1)

name: ALGM
backbones: ViT-T; ViT-S; ViT-B; ViT-L (Segmenter, SETR, SegViT); EVA (ViT-Adapter + Mask2Former)
main_result: Segmenter ViT-S ADE20K: mIoU 46.4 at 192 im/s, 26.3 GFLOPs (baseline 45.3 at 134 im/s, 38.6 GFLOPs); ALGM* 45.5 at 235 im/s, 20.9 GFLOPs
notes: Layer 1: CLAP average-pools the tokens of each 2x2 window whose mean pairwise cosine similarity exceeds tau. Layer 5 (7 for ViT-L): GBM, ToMe bipartite matching that keeps only edges above tau. tau = mean + std of token similarities on the training set, so the token count varies per image (ALGM* uses a lower tau at inference). Unmerging duplicates the merged embedding to the original indices, before a CNN decoder or after a transformer decoder. Main results re-train the segmentation network with ALGM; a training-free application to EVA + Mask2Former keeps mIoU at +26% throughput. Throughput on A100 with batch 32.
evidence: "CLAP merges only the tokens in windows w for which µw > τ , where τ is an automatically determined similarity threshold" (Sec. 3.3); "we deploy an unmerging module that duplicates the embeddings of the merged tokens at the indices of the tokens from which they were merged" (Sec. 3.3); "Using this threshold, the number of remaining tokens N ′ and N ′′ after the CLAP and GBM modules will vary per image." (Sec. 3.3); "The results in Tab. 4 show that without training, we can improve the throughput by 26% while keeping the mIoU constant. When we also train the model, we achieve the same efficiency gains but now also further improve the mIoU with +0.2." (Sec. 5.2)

name: AdaGlimpse
main_result: ViT-B encoder: ImageNet top-1 77.54 with 14 glimpses of 32x32 (28.57% of pixels; STAM 76.13); 76.30 with about 8.3 glimpses (16.94%) with early stopping
notes: Reinforcement learning (Soft Actor-Critic). The agent picks position and scale (x, y, z) of each glimpse in a continuous space; each glimpse is captured at a fixed d_cam x d_cam resolution and split into 16x16 patches, so the number of processed tokens is the number of glimpses so far times the patches per glimpse. Exploration stops at a maximum number of glimpses or when a confidence level is reached. The ViT-B encoder is pre-trained by the authors for 600 epochs with 196 random glimpses and then trained 100 epochs alternating backbone and agent; no external checkpoint is mentioned, so training is taken as from scratch. Teacher for distillation is a pre-trained DeiT III ViT. Also reconstruction (other) and ADE20K segmentation. No FLOPs or latency. Active visual exploration rather than token reduction inside a ViT.
evidence: "It uses Soft Actor-Critic, a reinforcement learning algorithm tailored for exploration tasks, to select glimpses of arbitrary position and scale" (Abstract); "The exploration process is stopped when a set confidence level or a maximum number of glimpses is reached" (3.1); "Additionally, we pre-train the model for 600 epochs with 196 random glimpses per image with sizes and positions sampled from a uniform distribution" (4. Training)

name: JMP
main_result: DeiT-S: 35% fewer FLOPs, more than 45% higher throughput, top-1 0.2 lower (ImageNet)
notes: [core] Per-sample choice between merging and pruning on DeiT-S with ImageNet numbers; full text not read. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. Tokens are split into critical and non-critical ones and the similarity between the two groups decides, per sample, whether non-critical tokens are merged or pruned; how critical tokens are scored and how many are kept is not said. No extra trainable parameters, but whether the model is fine-tuned is not said. Absolute DeiT-S accuracy, GFLOPs and throughput (and GPU) are not in the abstract.
evidence: "this work proposes a token compression framework: joint merging and pruning (JMP), which adaptively selects a better token compression strategy based on the similarity between critical tokens and non-critical tokens in each sample" (Abstract); "does not require the introduction of additional trainable parameters" (Abstract)

name: Token Adapter
main_result: Segmenter ViT-L/16 ADE20K: mIoU 52.02 at 273.0 GFLOPs / 15.09 FPS (baseline 51.82 at 658.98 GFLOPs / 10.68 FPS)
notes: Token injector: each row and column gets an importance score from the max over channels and then over the row/column; whole rows and columns (ratios r_h, r_w, e.g. 0.3) become normal tokens and are averaged into their most cosine-similar representative token, and some unique rows/columns are kept intact. Token ejector: after the wrapped blocks each original token is matched to the reduced tokens by the distance matrix and the sequence is rebuilt to full length. Applied to official checkpoints without training. FPS on one RTX 3090; batch size not stated. The abstract says the code will be released at the URL.
evidence: "we compress rows and columns with reduction ratios rh and rw respectively" (Sec. 3.1); "we first calculate the maximum value of each token vector (you can also calculate its sum value or range value instead)" (Sec. 3.2); "Normal tokens are injected into representative tokens, while unique tokens remain intact." (Sec. 3.2); "By following this approach, the reduced sequence can be efficiently reverted to its initial length." (Sec. 3.2); "The proposed module is inserted into two classic models off-the-shelf with no re-training or fine-tuning required." (Sec. 4.1)

name: PiToMe
backbones: DeiT-T/S/B; ViT-L/H (MAE); CLIP; ALBEF; BLIP; BLIP-2; LLaVA-1.5 7B/13B; BERT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.1 off-the-shelf and 79.8 after retraining at 2.9 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6); ViT-H (MAE) off-the-shelf 86.4 at 92.8 GFLOPs (baseline 86.9 at 167.4)
notes: Energy score per token = mean over the key-token graph of an ELU-like function of cosine similarity with a layer-dependent margin m; the 2k highest-energy tokens are mergeable, the rest protected; the mergeable set is split by sorted energy (odd/even) into A and B and matched by BSM; proportional attention. A fixed ratio r of tokens is kept per layer (k = N - N r). Both off-the-shelf and retrained settings; deits_top1 is the off-the-shelf value, retrained 79.8. Latency only as relative speed-ups and inference times for retrieval and LLaVA (five V100 / A100), no DeiT-S throughput. Also text classification with BERT.
evidence: "This score identifies large clusters of similar tokens as high-energy, indicating potential candidates for merging, while smaller (unique and isolated) clusters are considered as low-energy and preserved." (Abstract); "We opt for using the key vectors K = Xl WK in RNxh as node features of V" (Sec. 3.2); "r is the fraction of remaining tokens" (Sec. 3.1); "We focus on two settings: Off-the-Shelf Performance , where we evaluate the models' performance immediately after compression without training, and Retrained" (Sec. 4)

name: AT-EDM
main_result: SD-XL 1024x1024 MS-COCO 2017 (5k captions): FID 28.04 / CLIP 0.3209 at 4.1 TFLOPs per step (SD-XL 31.94 / 0.3284 at 6.7 TFLOPs); sampling 20.3 s vs 31.0 s without fused ops (1.53x)
notes: Tokens are latent feature-map tokens of the SD-XL U-Net attention blocks. Importance via G-WPR, a weighted PageRank over the self-attention map (no class token, hence cls-attention in the sense of attention statistics); the top-k tokens are kept after the first attention layer of each block (pruning ratio rho = 63% for the 4.1T budget). Before each ResNet block the pruned tokens are refilled by copying the retained token from which they receive the highest attention (similarity-based copy). DSAP: in the first 15 of 50 denoising steps the first down-stage and last up-stage attention blocks are left unpruned. With xFormers the speed-up is 15-18% because attention maps must be recomputed. Batch size for latency not stated.
evidence: "leverages attention maps to perform run-time pruning of redundant tokens, without the need for any retraining. Specifically, for single-denoising-step pruning, we develop a novel ranking algorithm, Generalized Weighted Page Rank (G-WPR), to identify redundant tokens, and a similarity-based recovery method to restore tokens for the convolution operation" (Abstract); "we only insert a pruning layer after the first attention layer of each attention block and set the pruning ratio for that layer to ρ. To meet the FLOPs budget of 4.1T, we set ρ = 63%." (Sec. 4.1); "We use the self-attention map to determine the source of the highest attention received for each pruned token and use that as the most similar one." (Sec. 3.2)

name: DTMFormer
main_result: SETR + DTMFormer: ACDC Dice 89.64 at 9.8 GFLOPs (SETR 88.56 at 53.2 GFLOPs)
notes: [application] Medical image segmentation (ACDC, ISIC, BTCV) with a plug-in token-merging transformer block. ATM picks the top rN center tokens by a dependence score (column sums of the attention map over half of the heads, with an L1 loss against ground truth) plus a DPC-KNN density-distance feature score; other tokens join centers by feature similarity and are merged with learned weights. LTR copies merged features back to the original token resolution. Sparsity ratio r is a fixed hyper-parameter (ablated 1/2 to 1/32). Networks are trained 400-600 epochs; the paper does not say whether transformer weights start from pre-training, so training is ?. Main goal is accuracy (attention collapse); GFLOPs only, no latency.
evidence: "DTMFormer consists of an attention-guided token merging (ATM) module to adaptively cluster tokens into fewer semantic tokens based on feature and dependency similarity and a light token reconstruction module to fuse ordinary and semantic tokens" (Abstract); "the top rN tokens (i.e., r is the sparsity ratio) with the highest scores are selected as center/semantic tokens for merging" (3.2); "LTR up-samples the token and recovers the feature mapping based on its merging history" (3.3)

name: GTPT
main_result: GTPT-S COCO-WholeBody: whole-body AP 59.6 at 1.99 GFLOPs (without pruning 59.4 at 3.53 GFLOPs)
notes: Whole-body pose estimation. Visual tokens are pruned in the coarse encoder by the attention of a human token and in the fine encoder per keypoint group (head, upper body, lower body) by softmax-pooled attention of the group's keypoint tokens; top (1 - alpha) N - N_d tokens kept per group. A global perceived loss distills the unpruned model into the pruned one (shared weights). Trained from random initialization for 300 epochs. The value of the pruning rate alpha is not in the main text. Only GFLOPs reported.
evidence: "each group takes their keypoint tokens as queries" (Sec. 3.5); "We can then select the top N̂v visual tokens and prune the remaining ones." (Sec. 3.5); "Random initialization without pre-training necessitates extended training epochs for fitting GTPT better." (Sec. 4.1)

name: RanMerFormer
notes: Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available; ScienceDirect blocked automated download and no preprint was found. Brain tumor MRI classification: a pre-trained ViT backbone with a token merging mechanism that removes redundant tokens, and a randomized vector functional-link (RVFL) head that trains quickly. How tokens are paired, how many are merged, whether the backbone is fine-tuned, the backbone names and all numbers could not be checked. Medical application paper.
evidence: "A pre-trained vision transformer is used as the backbone model. Then, a merging mechanism is proposed to remove the redundant tokens in the vision transformer, which improves computing efficiency substantially" (Abstract); "Finally, a randomized vector functional-link serves as the head in the proposed RanMerFormer, which can be trained swiftly" (Abstract)

name: Zero-TPrune
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M; AugReg ViT; MAE ViT; SWAG ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.4 at 2.97 GFLOPs (no fine-tuning; baseline 79.8 at 4.55)
notes: I-stage: the attention matrix is treated as a directed graph and a Weighted Page Rank (30/5/1 iterations by depth) gives importance scores; heads are combined by root-mean-square (EIR) and filtered by variance (VHF); the CLS token gets a larger initial score. S-stage: tokens are split by importance rank and one token of each of the top-r most similar pairs (cosine of keys) is pruned. Order I'-S-I. Retention rates per pruning layer are fixed hyperparameters (optionally searched by Monte Carlo). Throughput on one A100 with batch 512. Main results are training-free; a fine-tuned variant is shown in Fig. 6 and Supp. C. The code cell is the project page given in the paper. Code: the project page jha-lab.github.io/zerotprune gives no code.
evidence: "the first zero-shot method that considers both the importance and similarity of tokens in performing token pruning. It leverages the attention graph of pre-trained Transformer models to produce an importance distribution for tokens via our proposed Weighted Page Rank (WPR) algorithm" (Abstract); "We retain the top-k important tokens (k is determined by the retention rates and the total number of tokens)" (3.2); "We prune one token in each selected pair instead of merging them" (3.3); "Without any fine-tuning, Zero-TPrune reduces the FLOPs cost of DeiT-S by 34.7% and improves its throughput by 45.3% with only 0.4% accuracy loss" (Abstract)

name: GTP-ViT
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M; ViT-B/8; ViT-Medium-GAP
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.5 at 3.4 GMACs (P=8 tokens per layer, no finetuning; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Scores come from the attention map, not from the CLS token: regeneration difficulty (diagonal of attention) times broadcasting ability (received attention), max over heads, so it works without a CLS token. The P lowest tokens per layer are removed and their features are propagated (added with a weight alpha) to kept neighbours on a graph built once after embedding from spatial adjacency and cosine similarity (operation 'other' = graph propagation of pruned features into several kept tokens). Proportional attention and attention-map sparsification are added. Costs are GMACs. Throughput on an A6000 with batch 128. Main results are training-free; a 30-epoch finetuned variant is also reported (79.7 at 3.5 GMACs).
evidence: "GTP meticulously propagates less significant tokens' information to spatially and semantically connected tokens that are of greater importance" (Abstract); "we keep N - P tokens with the largest Gamma x Psi values and propagate the rest P tokens" (3.2.1); "GTP decreases the computational complexity of both DeiT-S and DeiT-B by up to 26% with only a minimal 0.3% accuracy drop on ImageNet-1K without finetuning" (Abstract); "we utilize the same data augmentation and training recipe as implemented in DeiT [38] and finetune for only 30 epochs" (4.1)

name: DeSparsify
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-T; T2T-ViT-19 (with ATS, AdaViT, A-ViT)
main_result: DeiT-S + ATS (ImageNet, 1,000 images): single-image attack raises GFLOPs from 3.09 to 4.20 (non-sparsified 4.6) at accuracy 88.2% (clean 88.5%); A-ViT reaches 4.6 GFLOPs, no token dropped
notes: Analysis (attack) paper, not a reduction method. Adversarial perturbations with a loss on each mechanism's keep decision make the input-adaptive token sparsification of ATS, AdaViT and A-ViT keep almost all tokens while the class prediction stays; the single-image attack recovers 74%, 44% and 100% of the GFLOPs that ATS, AdaViT and A-ViT save on DeiT-S, and on ATS raises GPU memory by 37% and energy by 72% (RTX 3090). A per-block upper bound on kept tokens is proposed as a defense (ATS: 4.2 to 3.17 GFLOPs under attack).
evidence: "we present DeSparsify, an attack targeting the availability of vision transformers that use token sparsification mechanisms" (Abstract); "The single-image attack variant, in which a perturbation is tailored to each image, results in the greatest performance degradation, increasing the GFLOPS values by 74%, 44%, and 100% for the ATS, AdaViT, and A-ViT, respectively." (Sec. 5.2); "an upper bound can be set to the number of tokens used in each transformer block" (Sec. 6)

name: RCTP
notes: [core] Retraining-free token pruning with per-block thresholds chosen for a FLOPs constraint; evaluation details are unknown. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. Token importance is Fisher information (gradient-based). A three-stage pipeline builds a candidate threshold table and a FLOPs-Fisher table, and a modified Viterbi algorithm picks the per-block threshold set with minimum Fisher loss for each FLOPs constraint in one shot. Pruning by threshold suggests the token count varies per image, but the abstract does not say. Datasets, backbones and numbers are not in the abstract. ISCAS paper; no hardware design is mentioned.
evidence: "we introduce Fisher information (FI) from tokens to evaluate token importance across different transformer blocks and propose a Retraining-free Constraint-aware Token Pruning (RCTP) framework" (Abstract); "a modified Viterbi algorithm determines optimal threshold sets with minimum overall FI loss under different FLOPs-constraints in one shot" (Abstract)

name: STAR
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.4 at 2.6 GFLOPs (STAR, rho=0.75; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Online [CLS] attention (intra-layer) is fused with offline LRP relevance (inter-layer, computed on training data) as a weighted product; top-k tokens are kept per layer. Per-layer keep rates are set offline from the average cosine similarity of tokens with one knob rho (same for every image). The a-STAR variant uses the rates as CDF percentiles, so the count varies per image (DeiT-S 79.3 at 2.5, 3843.7 img/s). Fine-tuned 120 epochs with hard distillation. Throughput on A100, batch 128, FP32. Code URL from the PDF hyperlink. Not RL.
evidence: "patches are successively pruned at each layer by maintaining only the top-k most important ones" (Abstract); "we propose an automated method for selecting them based on offline-derived metrics" (Abstract); "The pruned models are fine-tuned for 120 epochs with hard distillation" (Sec. 6)

name: ToC3D
backbones: ViT-B (SAM weights); ViT-L (EVA-02 weights); StreamPETR detector
main_result: ViT-B: nuScenes val NDS 55.2 with backbone time 70.3 ms (StreamPETR 55.4 at 85.2 ms), RTX 3090
notes: [application] Multi-view 3D detection on nuScenes with StreamPETR. In 3 blocks MQTS scores image tokens by attention to the top-N_q history object queries (with motion), followed by a linear layer and sigmoid, supervised by projected ground-truth boxes. The top rho N tokens go through the regular blocks with one score-weighted bridge token of the redundant tokens; redundant tokens take the identity path and receive the updated bridge token, so they stay in the sequence. Keep ratios (0.7, 0.5, 0.5) for Fast and (0.5, 0.4, 0.3) for Faster. Trained 24 epochs from SAM / EVA-02 weights. Inference time on one RTX 3090; batch size not stated.
evidence: "MQTS takes image tokens and history object queries as inputs, models the motion information of object queries, and calculates the importance score of each image token through the attention mechanism" (1 Introduction); "ρ is the pre-set constant keeping ratio of each block" (3.2); "we use more neural layers (i.e., regular path) to extract rich semantic and geometric information in salient tokens, while using shallow layers (i.e., free path, we use the identity layer in this paper) to keep the information in redundant tokens" (3.3)

name: DyT
main_result: ViT-B/16: VTAB-1K mean top-1 77.14 at 12.54 GFLOPs (r=0.5; full tuning 68.96 at 17.58)
notes: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method. A linear token dispatcher per block (threshold 0.5, Gumbel noise in training) decides which tokens enter the MLP; deactivated tokens skip the block and are processed only by a parallel adapter, so the token count is not reduced (operation other, closest to a per-block halt). Only adapters and dispatchers are trained (0.16 M parameters). 912.30 img/s on V100 at batch 512. Main purpose is efficient adaptation; token skipping is the inference-efficiency mechanism. Not RL.
evidence: "we propose a token dispatcher to distinguish informative tokens from less important ones, allowing the latter to dynamically skip the original block" (Abstract); "Then, we set 0.5 as the threshold to determine the activation of each token" (Sec. 3.2); "DyT does not reduce the total number of tokens, making it suitable for both visual recognition and dense prediction scenarios" (Introduction)

name: PRO-SCALE
backbones: Mask2Former with Swin-T; ResNet-50; MViTv2-T (also MaskDINO, open-vocabulary FC-CLIP style models)
main_result: Swin-T Mask2Former (COCO panoptic): PQ 52.82 at 171.7 GFLOPs, encoder 56.18 GFLOPs (M2F 52.03 at 234.5, encoder 117.0)
notes: [core] Token length reduction in the multi-scale transformer encoder of Mask2Former with a clear segmentation evaluation, but the backbone is a CNN or Swin and the tokens are encoder feature queries. The encoder has three stages: stage 1 sees only the smallest-scale tokens (s4), stage 2 adds s3, stage 3 adds s2, each repeated p1/p2/p3 times, so large-scale tokens skip the early encoder layers (operation other: tokens are added progressively, no token is scored). A light pixel embedding (max-pooling) replaces the convolutions on s1, and a token recalibration module enriches small-scale tokens. Same lengths for every image. The whole segmentation model is trained (COCO 50 epochs, Cityscapes 90k iterations) from ImageNet-pretrained backbones, as for Mask2Former; the encoder is not taken from a trained model (training scratch, as for Lite-DETR in g8). FPS on A6000 in the ablation table (Cityscapes); batch size not stated.
evidence: "The underlying principle of PRO-SCALE is: progressively scale the length of the tokens with the layers of the encoder." (Abstract); "gradually expanding the token length of inputs to intermediate layers in PRO-SCALE" (3.1); "For COCO, our models are trained for 50 epochs." (Appendix, training details)

name: FlexiDiT
backbones: DiT-XL/2; T2I Transf. (PixArt-style); Emu 1.7B DiT; Video DiT 4.9B
main_result: T2I Transf. 256x256 MS COCO: FID 14.71 / CLIP 25.58 at 58% of baseline FLOPs (baseline 14.75 / 25.60 at 100%); video: up to 75% less compute without a significant VBench drop
notes: One DiT is made to accept a second, 2x larger patch size (4x fewer tokens) through new embedding / de-embedding layers (projected with the pseudo-inverse of bilinear interpolation) and patch-size embeddings. The inference scheduler runs the first T_weak denoising steps with the large patch size and the rest with the original one (fixed rule, same for every image); the weak model can also serve as the guidance signal. Class-conditioned DiT-XL/2 is fully fine-tuned; T2I and video models keep frozen weights with per-patch-size LoRAs trained by distillation (backbone frozen). Results are reported mainly in FLOPs; latency appears only as relative latency of CFG packing variants (App., Fig. 12) and a roofline analysis on H100. No code URL in the paper.
evidence: "We instead propose to use different patch sizes at different steps in the denoising process of the same image." (Sec. 3); "by leveraging bigger patch sizes only for early steps, we can reduce the overall generation time while maintaining both low and high-frequency details in the produced images" (Sec. 3); "We obtain a flexible model — coined FlexiDiT — by modifying and fine-tuning a pre-trained DiT" (Sec. 3); "we freeze the original weights and add trainable LoRAs" (Sec. 3.2)

name: Cropr
main_result: ViT-L (MAE): top-1 85.3 at 1480 img/s (1.7x; baseline 85.8 at 860 img/s, A100); EVA-02-L 448px: top-1 89.7 at 0.18 TFLOPs (2.1x; baseline 89.9 at 0.31)
notes: A Cropr module after every block scores tokens with a single-head cross-attention scorer with learnable queries and keeps the Top-K (R tokens pruned per block, constant per image); an aggregator plus auxiliary task head train the scorer end-to-end (stop-gradient to the backbone) and are removed at inference, where the router reduces to a vector-matrix product. Last Layer Fusion reinserts all pruned tokens before the final block for dense tasks (ADE20k Segmenter, COCO Cascade Mask R-CNN). The backbone is fine-tuned together with the modules. Throughput on an A100 with AMP, best over batch sizes. No DeiT-S.
evidence: "we present a token pruner that uses auxiliary prediction heads that learn to select tokens end-to-end based on task relevance. These auxiliary heads can be removed after training" (Abstract); "The scorer itself is modeled after a cross-attention module with learnable queries" (3.1); "we use a throughput-optimized static approach that prunes a constant number of tokens to enable batching across inputs" (2); "pruned tokens from all Cropr modules are inserted alongside retained tokens output by the penultimate ViT block" (3.3); "We fine-tune ViT-L on ImageNet-1k using a pretrained masked autoencoder (MAE)" (4.1)

name: AgentViT
main_result: ViT: Imagenette+ accuracy 58.93 (vanilla 59.95); inference 0.332 GFLOPs and 561 FPS vs 0.675 and 291 (Table 7)
notes: Reinforcement learning (Double DQN). The state is the mean attention per patch from the first ViT layer; patches with Q-value above the mean Q-value are kept and the rest are dropped for the remaining layers. The reward mixes training loss and the number of selected patches. Small ViTs are trained from scratch together with the agent on CIFAR10, FashionMNIST and Imagenette+ (10 ImageNet classes); the stated main goal is shorter training time. Table 7 does not name its dataset. RTX A2000 GPU.
evidence: "For each training batch, the agent observes the attention values generated by the first ViT layer and selects a subset of the original patches to be used during the ViT training process" (Introduction); "selects those with Q-values exceeding the mean Q-value across all patches" (Sec. 3); "we simultaneously trained the underlying SimpleViT and the agent inside AgentSimpleViT" (Sec. 4.2)

name: SparseDiT
main_result: DiT-XL ImageNet 512x512: FID 3.13 at 235 GFLOPs, 0.685 img/s (DiT-XL 3.04 at 525 GFLOPs, 0.249 img/s), r in [0.90, 0.96], A100 batch 128
notes: Three segments: poolingformers (global average pooling of V instead of attention) in the bottom layers, sparse-dense token modules in the middle, dense transformers at the top. In each module M sparse tokens are initialized by adaptive spatial pooling of the dense tokens and refined by cross-attention to them, processed by sparse transformers, then upsampled, fused with the dense tokens and refined by a reverse cross-attention (resample + reactivate). No token scoring. The pruning rate r = 1 - M/N is held at r_min for the first T/4 steps and then changes linearly with the step (same rule for every image). Fine-tuned from pretrained DiTs (400K iterations for DiT-XL, about 6% of pretraining). No code URL found in the paper text.
evidence: "These sparse tokens can be initialized by adaptively pooling the dense tokens X." (Sec. 3.1); "Sparse token interact with full-size dense tokens via an attention layer to integrate the global information" (Sec. 3.1); "we utilize an attention layer to perform a reverse operation of the generation of sparse token to produce the restored dense tokens" (Sec. 3.1); "We exploit this by dynamically adjusting the pruning rate r across sampling steps, increasing tokens as sampling progresses." (Sec. 3.2); "Our method fine-tunes pre-trained DiT models to improve efficiency." (Sec. 3.3)

name: Dynamic DETR
backbones: ResNet-50; Swin-T (Deformable DETR, DAB-, DN-, H-Deformable DETR, DINO)
main_result: DINO ResNet-50 COCO (36 epochs): AP 50.2 at 141.7 GFLOPs / 23.2 FPS (DINO 50.9 at 244.5 GFLOPs / 14.4 FPS)
notes: Encoder tokens of multi-scale DETRs. The 6 encoder blocks form 3 stages; per stage the level retention ratios (e.g. 0.5/0.4/0.3/0.2) are reordered by an importance ranking of levels measured on COCO val (same for every image). Low levels: proximal aggregation averages the n x n windows with the highest mean cosine similarity into one token. Top level: holistic aggregation keeps tokens with low mean similarity to others and averages each other token into its top-T (=3) most similar kept tokens. A center-distance regularization aligns sparsified and dense features. Models are trained with the baseline recipes. FPS GPU and batch size not stated. No code link in the PMLR paper or page. Whether merged tokens still serve as keys is not stated.
evidence: "Within each stage, we apply a proximal aggregation paradigm for low-level tokens to maintain spatial integrity, and a holistic strategy for high-level tokens to capture broader contextual information." (Abstract); "Then unimportant tokens are aggregated into its most affine counterparts with the proposed affinity matching and aggregation mechanism." (Fig. 3); "we leverage statistic-based importance ranking to dynamically derive this key parameter for token sparsification at each level" (Sec. 3.2); "Note that the statistics are captured on the COCO val-set images" (Fig. 4); "To ensure fair comparisons, we strictly follow the configurations of baseline models, including hyperparameters, network architectures, and loss functions." (Sec. 4.1)

name: Representation Shift
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; UMT-B; UMT-L; ResNet-34; ResNet-50; Vision Mamba (ViM-T)
main_result: DeiT-S (ImageNet-1k, with FlashAttention): top-1 77.8 at 3.0 GFLOPs, 5948 img/s (baseline 79.8 at 4.6, 3002 img/s; class-attention pruning 72.1 at 3.0, 4844 img/s)
notes: [core] Training-free token pruning score that works with FlashAttention because it needs no attention map; evaluated on DeiT ImageNet and on UMT video-text retrieval and video QA (up to 5.5x speedup). The score is the L2 distance between a token before and after the MLP, i.e. the magnitude of the MLP update (criterion norm in the sense of an update magnitude, not the token norm). DeiT: 20% of tokens pruned at layers 1, 4, 7; UMT: 20% (retrieval) or 10% (QA) in each of the first three layers. Throughput on RTX A6000, batch 512 for DeiT, batch 20 for UMT. The ViT and video results are training-free; the ResNet variant (row/column pruning) is fine-tuned for 100 epochs, hence mixed. Also used as the importance metric inside vid-TLDR and on ViM.
evidence: "We compute the L2 distance between token representations before and after the MLP layer to quantify how much each token is emphasized by the transformation." (Fig. 2); "After quantifying the importance of the tokens in the [1,4,7] layers of DeiT, we pruned the 20% tokens at each layer." (4.2); "For vision transformers, we use DeiT [52] without additional training" (4.2); "we finetune the model for 100 epochs, including 10 cooldown epochs to refine this change" (4.2, ResNet)

main_result: DINOv2-G (AGX Orin, batch 2): top-1 -2.04 points at 104.1 ms (-33.1% latency; baseline 155.5 ms)
notes: Offline, for a model-device pair, latency L(n) is measured for every token count n and accuracy A(n) is estimated by random pruning after the first layer; the number of tokens R to prune maximises 0.5*U_A + 0.5*U_L, exploiting non-linear latency-workload steps (GPU tail effect). All R tokens are pruned once after the first 25% of layers. Tokens are ranked by received attention (max over heads) plus a V-matrix magnitude term; pruned tokens are averaged into one inattentive token as in EViT. DeiT-S results are given only as accuracy drop and latency (TX2 batch 2: -1.24 points at 49.44 ms; batch 1: -0.99 points at 32.12 ms), no absolute accuracy or FLOPs. The paper says the code is open source but gives no URL.
evidence: "we determine token pruning schedule by leveraging non-linear latency-workload relationships. Third, we demonstrate a training-free, token pruning method utilizing this schedule" (Abstract); "Our schedule prunes all R tokens at one layer, early in the model" (3.2); "we rank token importance by measuring the attention each token receives from all others, utilizing the softmax attention matrix. We also incorporate an importance term derived from the V matrix" (3.3); "instead of discarding pruned tokens, we create a new "inattentive" token based on the features of all pruned tokens" (3.3)

name: FR2ViT
main_result: Segmenter ViT-L: 1.95x FPS with 0.43% performance drop
notes: [core] Finetuning-free token reduction for dense prediction; full text not read. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. A high-order informativeness assessment splits tokens into superior and inferior ones; superior tokens get full attention ('refinement') and inferior tokens are processed by a cheaper reactivation branch, with light interaction between the branches, so every token stays active at a different cost. The scoring rule, the split ratio, the three dense tasks and other backbones are not in the abstract.
evidence: "we propose FR2ViT, a finetuning-free refinement-reactivation architecture for efficient vision transformers, allowing tokens of varying informativeness to activate softly at differing costs" (Abstract); "We refine superior tokens through extensive attention interaction, while inferior tokens undergo effective reactivation" (Abstract)

name: SDTM
backbones: SD3 Medium; SD3.5 Large; SD3.5 Large Turbo (MMDiT)
main_result: SD3 Medium 1024x1024 COCO2017 (50-step RF): FID 29.60 / CLIP 0.3224 at 7.07 s, 1.51x (baseline 29.02 / 0.3267 at 10.67 s); SDTM* (adaptive threshold) FID 28.97 at 6.90 s, 1.55x
notes: Two stages over denoising steps. Structure stage (first 40% of steps): windows with high mean cosine similarity (plus a priority for tokens not merged recently) are averaged into one token before MHSA and MLP. Detail stage: tokens with low received attention (inattentiveness from the attention map) are merged into their most similar attentive token before the MLP only. Merged tokens are restored by similarity-based copy blended with the previous step's features. Schedule: the default SDTM uses a hand-set cosine decay of the merge ratio over steps (same for every image); SDTM* uses a per-layer and per-step threshold from a calibration batch, so the count varies per image. Also reweights prompt tokens using categories from ChatGPT. Latency averaged over 5000 COCO images on A100 40G; batch size not stated.
evidence: "Served in a post-training way, the proposed method can be integrated seamlessly into any DiT architecture." (Abstract); "we compute the average cosine similarity within each window w as the similarity priority score" (Sec. 4.1.1); "Utilizing the attention map, which effectively quantifies the relationships between tokens, we identify the inattentive tokens." (Sec. 4.1.2); "This method offers a straightforward approach for dynamically adjusting the merging ratio." main_result: DeiT-S (DINO, ImageNet-1k linear eval): 62.31 at 76% training FLOPs (DINO baseline 62.49 at 100%; EViT 60.06, ToMe 60.34) with keep rate 0.8

main_result: 75% higher throughput, 40% fewer GFLOPs and up to 1.1 higher mIoU (backbone and dataset not in the abstract)

Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. Hierarchical Condition Pooling merges tokens in hierarchical local windows and Protected Bipartite Matching protects informative tokens (high average similarity to all other tokens) during global bipartite merging. A shared MLP actor makes a keep/prune decision for each token after blocks 3, 6, 9; rewards trade the number of kept tokens against correctness, so the count per layer and image is learned (alpha/beta sets the GFLOPs). The main table trains only the RL parts with the ViT fixed; optional alternating ViT fine-tuning improves accuracy (Fig. 4). Speed on one A6000 (batch size not stated).

name: ToMA
main_result: SDXL-base 1024x1024 (ImageNet class prompts): FID 28.88 / DINO 0.068 at 11.0 s/img on V100 (baseline 25.27 at 14.5 s/img), merge ratio 0.5 (about 24% faster); Flux.1-dev 23.4% faster at ratio 0.75 on RTX6000

(Sec. Vote&Mix); "we fine-tune VoMix from DeiT-S for 100 epochs" (Sec. Image Experiments)

name: CLCA
backbones: ViT-B/16 pre-trained as ViT, DeiT, DeiT3 (IN-1k and IN-21k), MIIL, MoCo v3, DINO, MAE, CLIP (LAION)
main_result: CLCA with EViT at 10% keep rate: SoyAgeing top-1 87.4 at 25.2 GFLOPs (ViT 67.0 at 78.5 GFLOPs)
notes: [application] Ultra-fine-grained leaf cultivar recognition (5 datasets) with an add-on for existing token reduction. Reduction is mainly EViT (top-k by [CLS] attention, rest fused into one token; also DynamicViT, ATS, SiT, PatchMerger, DPC-KNN, ToMe) at layers 4, 7, 10 of ViT-B/16. A Cross-Layer Cache stores GAP features and a register token after each block and appends them back after each reduction, and a Cross-Layer Aggregation head classifies from the CLS outputs of all groups. Keep rates 100 to 10%. Pre-trained backbones fine-tuned 50 epochs at image size 224 or 448. Table I does not say which backbone the CLCA rows use. FLOPs only.
