name: PruMerge / PruMerge+ (LLaVA-PruMerge)
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: PruMerge+ VQAv2 76.8 / POPE 84.0 / MME 1462.4 (baseline 78.5 / 85.9 / 1510.7) with 25.0% of visual tokens on average; PruMerge 72.0 / 76.3 / 1350.3 with 5.5%
notes: ICCV 2025 (arXiv v1 Mar 2024). Reduction at the vision-encoder output before the projector: CLS attention of the penultimate CLIP layer selects outlier tokens (IQR rule, so the count varies per image), pruned tokens are merged into the kept ones by kNN on last-layer keys with class-attention weights; PruMerge+ adds spatially uniform tokens. LLM untouched. Main Table 1 uses LoRA fine-tuning of LLaVA-1.5 for 1 epoch (light); training-free results in Table 6 and for Video-LLaVA. Table 2 prefill time is a roofline estimate on V100, not measured. No code URL in the arXiv text.
evidence: "we exploit the sparsity observed in the visual encoder, characterized by the sparse distribution of attention scores between the class token and visual tokens. This sparsity enables us to dynamically select the most crucial visual tokens to retain. Subsequently, we cluster the selected (unpruned) tokens based on their key similarity and merge them with the unpruned tokens" (Abstract); "we adopt the Interquartile Range (IQR) method [5] ... Any attention values residing outside these fences are classified as outliers" (Sec. 3.2); "PruMerge can be conducted in either a training-free or fine-tuning manner" (Sec. 4.4.3); "We further finetune LLaVA-1.5 using LoRA [19] for 1 epoch" (Sec. 4.1)

name: AsymRnR
backbones: CogVideoX-2B; CogVideoX-5B; Mochi-1; HunyuanVideo; FastVideo-Hunyuan; AnimateDiff
main_result: HunyuanVideo: VBench 0.8237 at 703.29 s, 1.30x (baseline 0.8157 at 912.98 s), fast setting, H100; CogVideoX-2B 1.17x at VBench 0.7849 (ToMe-fast 1.16x at 0.7732)
notes: Reduction is applied inside self-attention of video DiTs after the Q, K, V projections: Q and the K/V pair are reduced separately by ToMe-style bipartite soft matching with their own rates, attention runs on the shorter sequences, and only the Q sequence is restored to full length. Which feature, block and timestep is reduced is decided by thresholding a similarity map estimated in advance from arbitrary sampling (context-agnostic, so the schedule is the same for every prompt; mapped to learned-rate as an offline search). Matching results are cached for s = 5 steps. Latency on A100 (CogVideoX) or H100 (others); batch size not stated.
evidence: "We propose Asymmetric Reduction and Restoration (AsymRnR), a training-free and model-agnostic method to accelerate video DiTs." (Abstract); "Unlike previous works that focus on reducing H, we reduce Q and K&V independently" (Sec. 3.3); "it is sufficient to restore the Q sequence" (Sec. 3.3); "Fortunately, we can leverage the property that similarity patterns are context-agnostic, enabling the similarity distribution to be estimated in advance through arbitrary diffusion sampling." (Sec. 3.4)

name: DyMU
backbones: CLIP ViT-L/14-336 in LLaVA-1.5-7B; SigLIP ViT-B/16-384 in LLaVA-1.5; SigLIP-so400m in LLaVA-OneVision-7B (Qwen2)
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: DyMU-low keeps 89 +/- 27 of 576 visual tokens (-84.5%) at 97.5% of the baseline's average score over 9 benchmarks (61.5 vs 63.1); DyMU-high 394 +/- 57 tokens at 63.2
notes: DToMe = ToMe's bipartite matching on keys inside the vision encoder, but edges are kept when their similarity exceeds a per-layer threshold tau_i instead of taking the top r, so the number of visual tokens varies with image complexity; the thresholds are calibrated once, without training, by ranking edges over large batches of 250k images so that B*r_i edges are merged on average per layer. Virtual Token Unmerging reconstructs the full-length RoPE attention inside the LLM from the merged tokens plus a position map. No parameters, no fine-tuning. Evaluated only on VLM/video benchmarks, no DeiT-S or ImageNet. Only FLOPs of the attention block are given (Table 1) and the paper notes the wall-clock difference is marginal with PyTorch attention. Code via project page only.
evidence: "Dynamic Token Merging (DToMe) reduces the number of visual token embeddings by merging similar tokens based on image complexity" (Abstract); "We then apply a threshold tau_i to retain edges t -> t_B where S_i [t] > tau_i . Unlike [3], this thresholding operation leads to a variable number of retained edges" (Sec. 3.1); "our method dynamically adapts token compression to the content of the image and operates completely training-free" (Abstract)

name: LTM-Transformer
backbones: MobileViT-XS; MobileViT-S; EfficientViT-B1; ViT-S; ViT-B; Swin-T; Swin-B
main_result: ViT-S: top-1 81.55 at 3.70 GFLOPs and 18.2 ms per batch of 128 after 50 epochs of mask-module fine-tuning (ViT-S 81.20 at 4.30 GFLOPs, 22.5 ms)
notes: Every block maps its N attention-output tokens to P = ceil(rN) tokens (r = 0.7 in all blocks) by multiplying with a soft merging mask G (N x P). A learnable mask module builds G from the previous mask and the current tokens, designed from a variational upper bound of the IB loss. Each output token is a weighted average of all input tokens, so it is closer to resample than to pairwise merging. Two setups: fine-tuning with pre-trained weights frozen and only the mask modules trained (light), and training from scratch (scratch). ViT-S is the original ViT (ref. [35]), not DeiT-S. Inference time in ms per batch of 128 on one A100. Batch-size sweep is in the supplementary, which was not read. Also COCO detection (SSDLite) and instance segmentation (Mask R-CNN).
evidence: "The LTM block merges the N tokens of Z into P tokens with P < N by multiplying Z with the token merging mask G(ℓ) ∈ RN×P" (Sec. 3.1); "every target token is an informative weighted average of the original output tokens" (Sec. 1); "In all our experiments, we set the value of compression ratio r = 0.7 for all our LTM models." (Sec. 4.1); "In the fine-tuning process, the pre-trained weights are not updated and only the weights in the token merging mask modules, M(ℓ), are updated." (Sec. 4.1); "the fine-tuning setup and the training-from-scratch setup" (Sec. 4.1)

name: TCA
backbones: CLIP ViT-B/16; CLIP ViT-L/14; SigLIP ViT-B/16; SigLIP 2 ViT-B/16
main_result: CLIP ViT-B/16 (cross-dataset benchmark, 10 datasets): average top-1 68.69 at 15.45 GFLOPs with R=0.9 (CLIP 64.59 at 17.59; TDA 67.53; EViT 65.17 at 15.41; ToMe 64.88 at 15.31)
notes: [vlm?] Token condensation in the CLIP / SigLIP image encoder used as training-free test-time adaptation for zero-shot classification; reduction is a means for adaptation and also lowers GFLOPs. Tokens are ranked by class-token attention per head, using the current class token together with a domain anchor token (stored low-entropy class tokens of earlier test samples), and the averaged relative ranking across heads decides: the lowest tokens are pruned and a middle band of ambiguous tokens is merged into K=2 centres chosen by greedy k-centre coreset selection and averaging (operation cluster). A fixed fraction R of tokens is kept (R=0.9 or 0.7 in the main table). Logits are also corrected by the stored anchors. Batch size 1, A6000; only GFLOPs, no wall-clock time. No code link in the paper.
evidence: "Rather than passively discarding tokens, TCA condenses token representation by introducing reservoir-based domain anchor tokens for information-preserving token reduction and logits correction." (Abstract); "evaluates the token importance individually for each attention head with the consideration of saved domain anchor tokens" (3.4); "we propose a domain-aware token merging strategy to consolidate these tokens into more representative ones" (3.4); "Notably, our method is training-free, enabling rapid adaptation with minimal hyperparameter dependency." (4.1)

backbones: Stable Diffusion 2 (U-Net); PixArt-alpha (DiT); Zero123++ (multi-view); AnimateDiff v3 (video)
main_result: Stable Diffusion 2 768x768 MS-COCO 2014 (30k): FID 17.75 / CLIP 31.76 at r = 0.75 (ToMeSD 20.89 / 31.71; no merging 11.88 / 31.83); 5.8 s vs 8.5 s per image at r = 0.7 (A5000)
notes: No acronym (importance-based token merging). Tokens are the latent tokens of the diffusion backbone (U-Net transformer blocks or DiT layers; spatial and temporal attention layers for AnimateDiff). Importance = magnitude of the classifier-free guidance term from the previous timestep (no extra cost); the top (1-r)(1+p) tokens form a pool from which dst tokens are sampled and independent tokens are chosen, all other tokens are merged into their most similar dst token (bipartite soft matching, cosine similarity, averaging); merged locations are refilled with the processed dst tokens after the layer. Cross-attention maps work as an alternative importance. Latency equals ToMeSD. No code URL found in the paper text; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we propose an importance-based token merging method that prioritizes the most critical tokens in computational resource allocation, leveraging readily available importance scores, such as those from classifier-free guidance in diffusion models" (Abstract); "Next, we perform bipartite soft matching by computing pairwise cosine similarities between src and dst tokens." (Sec. 3); "The diffusion model layer then processes this reduced token set, the merged locations are filled with the corresponding processed dst tokens, maintaining the same output shape as the input." (Sec. 3); "The token merging ratio is r." (Sec. 3)

name: VisionZip
backbones: LLaVA-1.5-7B; LLaVA-1.5-13B; LLaVA-NeXT-7B; LLaVA-NeXT-13B; Mini-Gemini; Video-LLaVA
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: 94.0% of average score over 11 benchmarks with 64 of 576 visual tokens (training-free), 95.2% after projector tuning; LLaVA-NeXT-7B: prefilling 27.8 ms vs 218 ms with 160 of 2880 tokens
notes: CVPR 2025 (doi 10.1109/cvpr52734.2025.01843). Reduction at the vision-encoder output (layer -2 features) before the projector: dominant tokens chosen by CLS attention (mean received attention for SigLIP), remaining tokens merged by key similarity into contextual tokens; text-agnostic, LLM unchanged. Training-free by default; VisionZip-dagger tunes only the projector (light, 30 min on 8 A800). Efficiency on one A800-80GB; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we first select the dominant tokens, which receive significant attention and aggregate most of the image information. Then, to avoid missing small but potentially important details, we employ a token merging strategy, merging retained tokens based on their similarity to further extract informative contextual tokens" (Sec. 1); "Our method can be used in training-free, fine-tuning, or training from scratch" (Sec. 1); "we use minimal instruction tuning data to efficiently fine-tune the multimodal projector while keeping other components frozen" (Sec. 2.4)

name: ImagePiece
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.22 at 3891.9 img/s (DeiT-S 79.83 at 2531.1 img/s)
notes: [core] Token merging plus pruning for DeiT on ImageNet-1k. The bottom 30% tokens by [CLS] attention are split into two sets and merged by bipartite soft matching (0.08 x tokens per step); their [CLS] attention is then recomputed and the bottom 20% are discarded (keep 0.8). A conv stem (four 3x3 and one 1x1 conv) replaces the patchify stem, and models are trained from scratch for 300 epochs with the DeiT recipe, so the DeiT-S numbers are for a modified DeiT-S. Throughput on one RTX 3090; no FLOPs, batch size or code link in the paper.
evidence: "ImagePiece groups semantically insufficient (bottom-k) tokens to a level that convey meaning" (Introduction); "each token in group A is merged with the most similar token in group B using bipartite soft matching (Bolya et al. 2023)" (ImagePiece); "We train our model from scratch for 300 epochs" (Implementation details); "we set the pruning ratio r to 0.8, which results in discarding the bottom 20% of tokens" (Implementation details)

name: DiffCR
backbones: PixArt-Sigma (T2I); Lazy Diffusion (PixArt-alpha based inpainting DiT)
main_result: PixArt-Sigma 512x512 T2I (LAION-5B, 10K images): FID 10.68 / CLIP 0.238 at 13957 GFLOPs, 179.71 s per batch of 16 on A100 (fine-tuned PixArt-Sigma 11.93 / 0.242 at 17362 GFLOPs, 225.38 s), DiffCR-LT, ratio 20%
notes: Mixture-of-depths routing for DiTs: a linear+sigmoid router per layer scores tokens, the top-k pass the whole layer (attention and MLP) and the rest skip it and are concatenated back unchanged (halt). The keep ratio of each layer and of each timestep region is a learned scalar (differentiable via two neighboring 10% bins, MSE loss to a target ratio); at inference the nearest bin is used, same for every image. Inpainting models are fully fine-tuned; the T2I model is fine-tuned with a rank-32 LoRA plus routers. Latency on A100 with batch sizes 16 and 128. The paper links a project page (https://www.haoranyou.com/diffcr), no code URL in the text.
evidence: "each DiT layer includes a router that is fine-tuned jointly with model weights to predict token importance scores" (Abstract); "After passing through the routers, we select the top-k most important tokens for this layer’s processing, while the activations of other tokens are cached and concatenated with the layer outputs, bypassing the entire layer computation, including both attention and MLPs." (Sec. 3.2); "we simply select the nearest bin as the final compression ratio during inference, eliminating any overhead" (Sec. 3.3); "For the T2I task, we fine-tune the model using a LoRA adapter with a rank of 32" (Sec. 4.1)

name: SiTo
backbones: Stable Diffusion v1.5; Stable Diffusion v2 (U-Net)
main_result: SD v1.5 512x512 ImageNet (2,000 images): FID 26.31 at 1.37 s/img, 1.90x (baseline 27.64 at 2.61 s/img), RTX 4090; COCO30K FID 11.17 at 1.75x (baseline 12.32)
notes: Tokens are the latent tokens of the U-Net transformer blocks (self-attention by default). In each s x s region the token with the highest sum of cosine similarity to all tokens (plus Gaussian noise to vary the choice across steps) becomes a base token; the K non-base tokens most similar to a base token are pruned, the rest pass the layer, and pruned tokens are recovered by copying their most similar base token. Same count for every image. No calibration data. Latency on one RTX 4090; batch size not stated.
evidence: "SiTo selects the tokens that have the highest similarity to the base tokens as the pruned tokens." (Introduction); "SiTo feeds the unpruned tokens to the neural layers and recovers the pruned tokens by directly copying their most similar base tokens." (Introduction); "we propose to add Gaussian noise to the similarity of different tokens, which introduces randomness during base token selection" (Introduction); "we prune the same number of tokens for all the images in the same batch" (Pruned Token Selection); "SiTo has no training requirements and does not require any calibration data" (Abstract)

name: TF-ATM
main_result: MAE-H: 44.5% FLOPs reduction with 0.39% top-1 loss on ImageNet
notes: Only the publisher abstract was available (ACM DL refused automated access, no open-access or arXiv copy found), so schedule, other backbones, DeiT-S numbers, latency and code are unknown. Tokens whose patches are close to the median representation in the frequency domain (MF) are merged into their neighbours. The abstract says no retraining is needed.
evidence: "we develop a method that is mathematically formulated to merge tokens corresponding to patches that are close to the Median presentation in the Frequency domain (MF)" (Abstract); "Without any retraining, TF-ATM leads to significant improvements over the state-of-the-arts (SOTAs), with similar FLOPs (floating point operations)." (Abstract)

name: DyDiT
main_result: DiT-XL ImageNet 256x256: FID 2.07 at 57.88 GFLOPs, 5.91 s/image (DiT-XL 2.27 at 118.69 GFLOPs, 10.22 s/image), lambda = 0.5, 1.73x on V100
notes: Tokens are the latent image patches of the DiT. Spatial-wise Dynamic Token (SDT): a per-layer token router (linear + sigmoid, threshold 0.5; Gumbel-sigmoid and straight-through in training) lets easy tokens bypass only the MLP block; they stay in the sequence and in self-attention (gather / scatter), so the operation is halt. Also Timestep-wise Dynamic Width (head and channel-group routing per timestep), which is not a token method. A FLOPs-constrained loss drives the average cost to a target ratio lambda; the per-image count still varies. Fine-tuned from pretrained DiT with under 3% extra iterations (48k iterations, batch 256 for XL). Speed on a V100 32G with the optimal batch size per model. arXiv Oct 2024; the key uses 2025.
evidence: "we develop a Spatial-wise Dynamic Token (SDT) strategy, which identifies image patches where noise prediction is relatively "easy", allowing them to bypass computationally intensive blocks" (Sec. 1); "Therefore, SDT is applied only in MLP blocks in each layer." (Sec. 3.3); "We then convert it into a binary mask Mtoken using a threshold of 0.5." (Sec. 3.3); "Our DyDiT can be built easily by fine-tuning on pre-trained DiT weights." (Sec. 4)

name: ToCa
main_result: PixArt-alpha (20 DPM++ steps) COCO2017: FID-30k 28.33 at 5.78 TFLOPs, 1.93x by FLOPs, 0.390 s (baseline 28.09 at 11.18 TFLOPs, 0.682 s), N = 3, R = 70%; OpenSora 2.36x at VBench 78.34 (baseline 79.13)
notes: Feature caching, not sequence shortening: in steps between full computations (every N steps), R% of the tokens in each cross-attention and MLP layer skip computation and reuse their cached output from an earlier step, while all tokens stay in the sequence, so halt is the closest operation. Self-attention layers are fully cached. Caching score from self-attention influence on other tokens and cross-attention entropy (attention statistics) plus cache frequency and a spatial-uniformity rule. Cache ratio is hand-set per layer depth and type (same for every input). Speed-up in Table 1 is by FLOPs; latency on A800 80GB, batch size not stated.
evidence: "we introduce token-wise feature caching, allowing us to adaptively select the most suitable tokens for caching, and further enable us to apply different caching ratios to neural layers in different types and depths" (Abstract); "In the following timesteps, we can skip the computation of some unimportant tokens by re-using their value in the cache C." (Sec. 3.4); "We firstly pre-define the cache ratio R of tokens in each layer" (Sec. 3.4); "estimated with an attention score in self-attention" (Sec. 3.5); "with no requirements for training" (Abstract)

name: TREWA
notes: [core] Wavelet-based token reduction for ViTs with comparisons to pruning methods; full text not read. Only the abstract was available (from the record in the authors' institutional repository iris.univpm.it; the PDF there needs a login, Springer blocked automated access, no arXiv copy), so the values below rest on the abstract. A DWT is applied to the token embeddings and only the low-frequency coefficients go to the next attention layer, dropping 50-75% of the tokens; the new tokens are DWT coefficients rather than a subset or average of the old ones, so operation is 'other'. For each image the level is chosen by comparing its attention entropy with that of the batch. Four datasets, pre-trained and from-scratch settings (whether the pre-trained setting is fine-tuned is not said).
evidence: "It then applies the DWT to the token embeddings and forwards only the low-frequency coefficients (i.e., those capturing the image’s main semantic structure) to the next attention layer, discarding 50–75% of the tokens." (Abstract); "For each image in a batch, TREWA selects a pruning level by comparing that image’s attention entropy with the batch one." (Abstract); "We evaluate TREWA on four benchmark datasets in both pre-trained and training from scratch settings" (Abstract)

name: Co-Me
main_result: VGGT (DTU-MVS depth, 32 frames): L1 1.10 cm at 788 ms, 7.73x vs VGGT 6094 ms (memory-efficient VGGT* 1266 ms, L1 0.89; FastVGGT 2003 ms) on H100; up to 16.2x on RealEstate-10K with 128 frames
notes: [application] Token merging for visual geometric transformers (VGGT, Pi3, DA3, MapAnything) in depth, pose and point-map estimation. A light confidence predictor (MLP, single-head attention, Conv2D) is distilled from the frozen model's own confidence map with a ranking loss (TartanAir, under one H100 hour) and placed in the middle of the encoder. Tokens are split into fixed groups of 3x3; a group whose mean predicted confidence is below the p-th percentile over the sequence (p=0.5) is averaged into one token for the remaining blocks (attention and MLP, with an attention bias log n) and split back before the head. The fraction is fixed per sequence but can differ between images. The base model is never updated. Latencies on H100 (also Jetson Thor and RTX 5090); single-frame latency is given for NYUd-v2 and ETH3D. Project page co-me-tokens.github.io; no code repository named in the paper.
evidence: "distilled a light-weight confidence predictor to rank tokens by uncertainty and selectively merge low-confidence ones" (Abstract); "For each group, if the average confidence falls below the p-th percentile across all groups in the image sequence, it is marked for merging." (3.2); "Importantly, we never update or back-propagate through the visual geometric model" (3.1)

name: NASTrack
backbones: OSTrack ViT supernets (tiny, small, base; base initialized from MAE ViT-B): NASTrack-T; NASTrack-S; NASTrack-B
main_result: NASTrack-T: LaSOT AUC 64.2 at 1.3 GFLOPs, 62 fps on Jetson Orin NX (OSTrack 69.1 at 21.5 GFLOPs, 18 fps); NASTrack-B 68.6 at 14.8 GFLOPs
notes: [core] Single object tracking: one-shot NAS on an OSTrack-style one-stream ViT where the per-layer token keeping ratio (1, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6) is a search dimension next to depth, width, heads and MLP ratio, so the ratio is fixed per searched subnet and the same for every frame. A blacklist removes keep-ratio patterns whose subnets collapse (low IoU with reasonable Params) and a Token Overlap Ratio picks a distillation teacher from an elite pool. The paper does not say how tokens are scored for pruning (it refers to 'importance scores' and builds on OSTrack, whose candidate elimination uses template attention), so criterion is '?'. Supernets trained 300 epochs on tracking data from MAE-pretrained ViT-B. Speed on RTX 4070 laptop GPU, Jetson Orin NX and i7-14700HX CPU; batch size not stated. Searched keep ratios match EViT and PPT pruning at the same architecture (Table 7).
evidence: "This framework incorporates token pruning to optimize both transformer block structures and the layer-wise token keeping ratio" (Abstract); "We incorporate the keeping ratio into the search space and utilize NAS to automatically find the optimal keeping ratio for each layer." (3.1); "We train the model using the OSTrack [Ye et al., 2022] framework, which adopts the Vanilla ViT-Base [Dosovitskiy et al., 2021] model as the backbone, pre-trained with MAE [He et al., 2022]" (4.1)

name: APT
backbones: ViT-B/16; ViT-L/14; ViT-H/14 (MAE); LLaVA-1.5-7B; LLaVA-1.5-13B (vision encoder); EVA-02-B; EVA-02-L (detection, segmentation)
main_result: ViT-L/14 at 224: ImageNet top-1 87.8 at 44.5 GFLOPs and 993 img/s after 1-epoch fine-tuning (ViT-L 87.9 at 59.7 GFLOPs, 883 img/s)
notes: Tokenization-type method. Pixel-intensity entropy is computed on the input image at several patch scales, and regions below a per-scale entropy threshold get a larger patch (32 or 64 px), so the token count varies per image and is fixed before the first block. Larger patches are embedded by resizing plus a zero-initialized MLP over the sub-patch embeddings, and variable lengths are handled by sequence packing. Main results fine-tune (full MAE recipe, or 1 epoch from a fine-tuned checkpoint). An ablation (Table 7) also reports accuracy without training. Throughput on a single GPU (ImageNet on an A100 node), batch size not stated. Criterion other = image entropy. Official ICLR title differs from the arXiv title (see g7_bib_notes.md). No DeiT-S.
evidence: "APT computes entropy at multiple scales and assigns larger patch sizes to regions with the lowest entropy, resulting in significantly fewer input tokens" (Sec. 1); "We then retain all such patches with entropy below a fixed threshold τi , which is a tunable hyperparameter for each level." (Sec. 3.1); "Since APT is content-aware, the number of tokens for each image can vary widely." (Sec. 3.3); "we observe that just one epoch is sufficient to “heal” the degradation from the new patchification scheme and match the original performance of the model" (Sec. 4.2)

main_result: ViT-B/16 (MAE): ImageNet top-1 80.8 at about 10 GFLOPs (about 0.5 above ToMe and ToFu at the same budget, SNR 20 dB)
notes: Not RL: the per-layer cosine-similarity thresholds tau_l in [0.5, 1] are searched offline by multi-objective Bayesian optimization (Gaussian process + EHVI) on 500 ImageNet images, giving Pareto policies over accuracy, GFLOPs and number of transmitted tokens. ToMe-style alternating source/destination split; a source token merges into its most similar destination only if the similarity is at least tau_l (norm-weighted average), so the token count varies per image. The merged tokens are sent over a noisy channel with a SwinJSCC encoder (semantic communication). VQA at 55 GFLOPs: ScienceQA 69.9, GQA 61.8 (LLaVA 70.4 / 62.0 at about 191 GFLOPs). Read arXiv v1 (submitted version), not the published OJ-COMS text. Code 'will be made available' per the paper.
evidence: "This paper introduces a training-free framework for adaptive token merging, a novel mechanism that compresses transformer representations at runtime by selectively merging semantically redundant tokens under per-layer similarity thresholds" (Abstract); "We cast the discovery of merging strategies as a multi-objective optimization problem and leverage Bayesian optimization to obtain Pareto-optimal trade-offs" (Abstract); "This condition makes the number of merged tokens inherently data-dependent" (V. Methodology)

name: Dyna-ViT
main_result: ViT-B/16: ImageNet-1k top-1 82.3 at 13.40 GFLOPs, 313 img/s (K=70%; baseline 81.8 at 19.90, 210 img/s; supplementary)
notes: Before the encoder each 16x16 patch is scored by a parameter-free proxy (default L2 norm of the raw patch; Sobel and entropy in ablations) and only the top-K% patches (K=70) plus [CLS] are embedded into an unmodified ViT. The paper calls the method training-free, but all reported models are fine-tuned 5-10 epochs with the pruning in place from the ImageNet-21k checkpoint (ImageNet-1k: 10 epochs); top-K indices are precomputed per split. Main experiments on PASCAL VOC (5 classes), CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet; ImageNet-1k only in the supplement. Throughput on one T4 with AMP (batch not stated). The VOC DynamicViT baseline (46.0%) looks like a failed run. No code URL. Not RL.

name: Vision-MoR

name: SRE-Merge
main_result: TransReID ViT-B/16 (Market-1501): Rank-1 95.8 / mAP 89.2 at 15.53 GFLOPs, 416.62 img/s (TransReID 95.6 / 89.3 at 20.41 GFLOPs, 335.73 img/s; ToMe 94.9 / 88.6) on A100

name: BiGain
main_result: Stable Diffusion 2.0 (ImageNet-1k, 70% merge ratio): diffusion-classifier accuracy +7.15 and FID 0.34 better than ToMe
notes: [generation] Training-free token compression for diffusion models that is judged both on generation (FID) and on diffusion-classifier accuracy (class-conditional denoising error). Two operators: (1) Laplacian-gated token merging: a Laplacian filter on the hidden-state grid scores local frequency, the lowest-scoring token in each stride becomes a destination, and source tokens merge into destinations by bipartite matching on similarity, with unmerge afterwards (as in ToMeSD); (2) Interpolate-Extrapolate KV downsampling: keys and values are pooled with a mix of nearest and average pooling while queries stay intact (operation other). A blockwise adaptive merging variant pools s x s blocks under a quantile threshold. Fixed merge ratio or downsampling factor. Only FLOPs, no wall-clock time.
evidence: "Laplacian-gated token merging, which encourages merges among spectrally smooth tokens while discouraging merges of high-contrast tokens, thereby retaining edges and textures" (Abstract); "present BiGain, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that preserves generation quality while markedly improving classification in accelerated diffusion models" (Abstract); "In each spatial stride, the lowest-scoring token is selected as a destination token, while the others form the source set." (Fig. 1)

name: RAS
main_result: SD3 1024x1024 COCO: FID 31.99 / CLIP 30.64 at 1.45 img/s with 7 steps and 25% sampling ratio (RFlow 5 steps: 39.70 / 29.84 at 1.43 img/s); up to 2.36x (SD3) and 2.51x (Lumina-Next-T2I) speed-up
notes: At each denoising step only the fast-update tokens are passed through the DiT; the other tokens reuse the noise predicted at the previous step and stay in attention as cached keys and values, so halt is the closest operation (a per-token feature cache across steps). Token score = standard deviation of the previous step's predicted noise per patch times exp(k x drop count). Top tokens by a user-set sampling ratio; the first steps are dense, the ratio is then reduced and some dense steps are inserted (hand-set rule). Throughput on one A100 80GB; batch size not stated. No code URL in the paper text.
evidence: "we introduce RAS, a training-free sampling strategy that dynamically adjusts update ratios across image regions based on model attention" (Abstract); "Only these regions are forwarded through the Diffusion Transformer (DiT) for denoising, while the remaining slow-update regions reuse the cached noise from the previous step." (Sec. 1); "features from slow-update regions are retained as reference keys and values for subsequent attention computations" (Sec. 1); "we analyze the model’s noise output and observe that the standard deviation of predicted noise effectively distinguishes different semantic regions" (Sec. 3.2); "the initial few steps (e.g., the first 4 out of 28) are executed with a full 100% sampling ratio to preserve the global image outline, after which the ratio is gradually reduced as the generation stabilizes" (Sec. 3.3)

backbones: Segmenter with DeiT-B; NViT-pruned DeiT-B (with ToMe, ALGM, CTS)
main_result: DeiT-B Segmenter (ADE20K, about 3.7x fewer FLOPs): ToMe 23.94 clean / 16.86 corrupted mIoU at 35.08 GFLOPs, NViT-S pruning 45.30 / 32.86 at 33.82, prune-then-merge 45.71 / 34.33 at 34.84 (baseline 47.22 / 35.58 at 129.70)

evidence: "we benchmark representative token compression and structural pruning methods for ViT-based semantic segmentation under matched FLOPs" (Abstract); "token compression is highly effective at mild reductions but degrades sharply when compression becomes severe" (Abstract)

name: MPM
backbones: ViT-T/16; ViT-S/16; ViT-B/16; ViT-B/8; ViT-L/16 (Segmenter); DeiT-B; EVA-01 (ViT-Adapter + Mask2Former)
main_result: Seg-S/16 (ADE20K): mIoU 45.1 at about 54 GFLOPs, 431 FPS (baseline 45.3 at 76.9 GFLOPs, 333 FPS; ToMe 45.5 at about 59, 388 FPS) on H100, batch 32

main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.7 at 3.0 GFLOPs (rho=0.7; baseline 79.8 at 4.6); 79.5 at 2.8

name: LiteVGGT
main_result: VGGT (ScanNet-50, 1000 images): Chamfer distance 0.428 at 127.2 s (VGGT* 0.485 at 1275.1 s; FastVGGT 0.436 at 258.3 s) on H20, with fine-tuning and FP8

name: CAIT
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT; Swin-T; Swin-S
main_result: DeiT-S (ImageNet-1k): top-1 80.2 at 2.1 GFLOPs, 1.9x throughput (baseline 79.8 at 4.6; VTC-LFC 79.8 at 2.1, 1.1x), with channel pruning included

name: HTTM
main_result: VGGT (NRGBD, stride 10): accuracy 0.012 / completeness 0.010 at 6.8 s with Q kept 20%, K/V 30% (VGGT* 0.010 / 0.010 at 13.9 s; FastVGGT 0.016 / 0.013 at 7.0 s); 1000 frames 102.8 s vs 724.6 s (7x) on A100
notes: [application] Training-free merging in the global attention layers of VGGT for multi-view 3D reconstruction. Queries and keys are merged separately in every attention head (values follow the keys) by ToMeSD-style src/dst matching on cosine similarity, attention runs on the shorter sequences, and the outputs are unmerged per head before concatenation. Tokens are reordered into spatio-temporal blocks (128 spatial tokens x 30 frames) and matching runs only inside a block; 10% outlier tokens with large deviation are excluded from merging under a global budget. name: TinyDrop
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16; BEiTv2-L; DeiT3-L (guidance: EfficientFormerV2-S2; EfficientNetV2-rw-t)
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.6 at 1.4 GFLOPs incl. guidance model and early exit (baseline 79.8 at 4.6); ViT-L/16: 85.2 at 9.6 (baseline 85.8 at 61.6)
notes: [core] Training-free token dropping for ViT classification with ImageNet results on DeiT-S and large ViTs. A small CNN or ViT guidance model runs first: if its max softmax confidence c exceeds tau the image exits with the guidance prediction, otherwise a Grad-CAM saliency map from the guidance model, resized to the ViT grid, selects the top-K patch tokens once before the first block of the frozen target ViT (positional embeddings and relative position bias are sliced). Drop ratio r = min(r_max, r_max (c/tau)^gamma) with gamma=0.5, r_max=0.7, so the count depends on the image. Reported GFLOPs are averages that include the guidance forward, the Grad-CAM backward and the early exits; on DeiT-S the early-exit-only ablation (w/o token dropping) already reaches 79.6% at 1.8 GFLOPs, while token dropping alone gives 79.1% at 3.0, so much of the saving comes from the exit. Which guidance model the Table 2 rows use is not stated. No latency; no code link in the paper. Read arXiv v1.
evidence: "we propose TinyDrop, a training-free token dropping framework guided by a lightweight vision model" (Abstract); "We compute token-wise saliency maps for the guidance model Mg by applying Grad-CAM [16] to the feature maps of its final transformer block" (2.1.2); "To adaptively determine the proportion of tokens to discard, we introduce a parametric confidence-to-drop mapping function" (2.1.3); "Low-importance tokens are discarded before the first transformer block of the target ViT" (2. name: SAD-TM
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; MAE-B; MAE-L; MAE-H; LV-ViT-S

notes: Importance = 0.5 x class attention (head average, computed at inference) + 0.5 x saliency outlier score. The lowest-score tokens are merged into the most similar candidate token by an importance-weighted average. Fixed merging rate per layer. The SAD-TM-DM variant skips merging in the first ceil(rho L) blocks (rho in [0.25, 0.35]) and gives DeiT-S 79.71 at 3.0 GFLOPs. FLOPs only (evaluation on an RTX 3090, batch 128). The paper says the code will be available soon.
evidence: "SAD-TM simply employs a fixed merging rate mr per layer for SAD-TM, i.e., a consistent proportion of tokens is merged in each block of the ViT." (Sec. 3.2); "the saliency map [24] for each input patch xi is computed via backward propagation" (Sec. 3.2); "we perform a weighted sum of the attention score with the saliency outlier score to obtain the final importance score" (Sec. 3.2); "our proposed SAD-TM and SAD-TM-DM do not require any training or fine-tuning" (Sec. 4.2)

name: ToFe
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 77.7 at 2.0 GFLOPs (baseline 79.9 at 4.6)

notes: Plug-in calibration that replaces proportional attention in an existing reduction method (ToMe, PiToMe, DiffRate, ToFu, DCT): merged values are scaled by sqrt(r) and merged logits are shrunk toward ln N_j with weight sqrt(r). The method has no token scoring of its own, so criterion and schedule come from the host method (bipartite similarity matching with a retention ratio r per layer for ToMe/PiToMe). ImageNet results are only in figures. The only DeiT-S table (Table 5) uses ToMe-trained DeiT-S weights with radial correction only (77.4 at 20 merged tokens per layer, no FLOPs). Latency = total evaluation time on the retrieval sets.
